fields.label: Cause
fields.value: Breaking the Angel Veyn Vow (betraying their own sworn promise).

fields.label: Markings
fields.value: Plain black spots or black cherry spotting depending on how much Veyn surged through when the vow broke.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Fallen Angels

fields.label: Sanctuary Break
fields.value: When an angel breaks their Vow through the deliberate betrayal of someone they swore to protect, a void forms in their Veyn channel. Corrupted Veyn seeps into this void over time, consuming their memories, emotions, and sense of self. Progressive descent into madness and evil.

fields.label: Sanctuary Break Stages
fields.value: Stage 1 — The Hollow (emptiness). Stage 2 — The Fog (memory loss, paranoia, violence). Stage 3 — The Hunger (Veyn-draining compulsion, loss of empathy). Stage 4 — The Hollowing (personality death, entity consumes Veyn mindlessly).

fields.label: Ordinary vs. Betrayal Break
fields.value: Ordinary break (weakness, doubt): standard Fallen Angel, stable. Betrayal break (using trust to destroy): triggers Sanctuary Break, progressive madness.

fields.label: Wener Leger's Break
fields.value: Wener broke his Vow through ordinary failure — general loss of faith, not betrayal of a specific person. He did not trigger a Sanctuary Break. He remained intact, intelligent, and capable. A Fallen Angel who breaks through doubt becomes Wener Leger — arguably worse than a Hollowed.

fields.label: Clint's Knowledge
fields.value: Clint Ashborn ordered Ordium's execution partly because Ordium's Vow was about protecting the Angel Realm's integrity. Breaking it through a hybrid child was a betrayal of the exact promise he swore to uphold. Clint knew the Sanctuary Break would have consumed Ordium within a year.

fields.label: Lore Connections
fields.value: Angel Veyn Vow, Thalor Elwin, Clint Ashborn, Ordium, Wener Leger, Dark Moon, Hollowed entities, Divine Weapons, Elyndor Academy.

fields.label: Wener Leger Example
fields.value: Wener broke his Vow through ordinary failure — general loss of faith. No Sanctuary Break. He remained intact, intelligent, and arguably more dangerous than a Hollowed.

fields.label: Ordium Would Have Hollowed
fields.value: Ordium's Vow was about protecting the Angel Realm's integrity. Creating a hybrid child was a betrayal of that promise. Clint knew the Sanctuary Break would have consumed Ordium within a year.

name: The Angel Veyn Vow
subtitle: A promise, spoken at the altar
description: Every angel takes the Veyn Vow when their halo first forms, at the Sundering Altar, at the age of fifteen. It is not an oath of obedience and not a chain — it is a promise, spoken freely, and the words of it are a ritual. Each angel’s vow is their own: a promise of what they will uphold, the truth they choose to carry, sworn into their own halo with the help of the Guardian — Thalor Elwin, the Fifth Pillar, who keeps the Sundering Altar. The halo is the physical seal of that promise, and it is what lets an angel’s Veyn flow steady and pure — because it is their own word, kept, that stabilizes them, not any master’s command. The vow is why angels can hold as much power as they do; without it their body cannot safely filter raw Veyn on its own. The stronger and truer the promise, the brighter the halo. It breaks only when an angel betrays their own sworn word.

fields.label: Incantation
fields.value: With this light I make my promise. By the Veyn that made me and the will that holds the world, I swear to keep the word I speak, and to carry my own truth until my light goes out. This halo is my seal — my promise made visible. May it hold while my word is true, and may it shatter the day I betray it.

fields.label: Halo
fields.value: The halo forms at age 15, at the Sundering Altar, when the vow is spoken with the Guardian’s help — Thalor Elwin, the Fifth Pillar.

fields.label: Nature
fields.value: A personal promise, not an oath of obedience — each angel swears their own truth.

fields.label: Seal
fields.value: The halo is the seal of the angel’s own word; keeping the promise keeps the Veyn steady.

fields.label: Breaking
fields.value: The vow breaks when an angel betrays their own promise — not by disobeying a superior, but by breaking their own word.

name: Demons (Overview)
subtitle: Four ranks — power, not profession
description: There are four ranks of demons: Mordrach, Bloodward, Scourge, and Gnash. They have horns on their forehead and feathery black wings. The number of horns and wings both indicate their rank — the higher the rank, the more horns and wings they have. They always have a demonic aura around them. A rank measures how much power a demon holds, not what they do for a living. Only some demons join the army; most are ordinary civilians — laborers, traders, craftsmen, and workers — who simply happen to hold their rank. Demons of any rank can leave the Demon Realm and live in the Human Realm as normal citizens, hiding their true nature behind Duskveil. Note: a rank can be passed down to an offspring, though not all the time, so they would have to work their way up the ranks.

fields.label: Note
fields.value: Both demons and angels can retract or hide their wings if they want.

fields.label: Duskveil
fields.value: Innate to all demons. Lets them blend into any society, hiding their true form and aura. The higher the rank, the more effective the disguise and the less power it costs; the lower the rank, the weaker the disguise and the more it cuts into their true strength.

fields.label: Six Fingers
fields.value: The Demon Realm's six generals are known as the Six Fingers — Bloodward-rank demons who bear titles named after the deadly sins (Pride, Greed, Lust, Sloth, Gluttony, Wrath). They mirror the Angel Realm's Six Pillars, which are named after Greek gods.

name: Mordrach
subtitle: Rank 1 — Rulers of the Demon Realm
description: The highest rank of demon — a tier of power so vast that the Mordrach rules the Demon Realm. They can’t be killed by regular weapons or holy imbued weapons. They can only be harmed and killed by a Divine weapon.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: 8 horns and 8 wings, the horns curling back and fused together at the base like a crown. Their wings are massive, tattered at the edges but still powerful, the black feathers seeming to absorb light rather than reflect it. They have the strongest aura amongst all the demons. Deep-purple colored wings.

fields.label: Skills
fields.value: Death Scythe, Chain Reaper Scythe, Call of the Dead, Dominating Will, Soul Oath, Veyn Decomposition (Mordrach), Hands of Death, Purgatory Flames, Charm, Soul-Sight, Berserk (Mordrach), Demonic Aura (Mordrach), Duskveil (Mordrach) — each skill has its own entry in the Angel Skills / Demon Skills categories.

fields.label: Known Mordrach
fields.value: Tera Morage (Female) — current ruler of the Demon Realm.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Fiends

name: Bloodward
subtitle: Rank 2 — The realm’s elite
description: A high-ranking demon of the second tier. Many Bloodwards command the Demon army, but not every Bloodward is a soldier — some are powerful civilians who hold the rank through strength alone. Their regenerative ability is less than the Mordrach, and their regenerative ability runs on Veyn.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: 6 horns and 6 wings, the horns sharp and jagged, some cracked from old battles. Their wings are broad and scarred, mirroring how the Aetherblade Lord Angel’s wings carry battle-scars that never fully heal. They carry themselves like commanders, always poised for a fight. Their aura is strong but not too strong like the Mordrach. Dark, purple colored wings.

fields.label: Skills
fields.value: Blood Chains, Warcry of Dominion, Crimson Ward, Blood Pact, Veyn Decomposition (Bloodward), Demonic Aura (Bloodward), Berserk (Bloodward), Duskveil (Bloodward) — each skill has its own entry in the Angel Skills / Demon Skills categories.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Dregs

name: Scourge
subtitle: Rank 3 — The mid ranks
description: A mid-ranking demon. The soldiers of the Demon army are drawn from the Scourge, but most Scourges are civilians — laborers, traders, and ordinary demons who simply hold this rank. They have a lesser regeneration that runs on Vitality.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: 4 horns and 4 wings, shorter and less refined than the ranks above. Their wings are smaller, feathers rougher and less full. Their aura is just normal. Wine purple colored wings.

fields.label: Skills
fields.value: Vitality Surge, Rend Claws, Pack Tactics, Veyn Decomposition (Scourge), Berserk (Scourge), Demonic Aura (Scourge), Duskveil (Scourge) — each skill has its own entry in the Angel Skills / Demon Skills categories.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Dregs

name: Gnash
subtitle: Rank 4 — The common demons
description: The lowest and most common rank of demon. At the age of 15 they are taken to The Sundering Altar for their awakening. They can make contracts with anyone, and once the contract is signed, they are bound by it and can’t break free from it until it has been fulfilled. Making a contract with a Gnash is very risky since most of the time they are not friendly, and they want to increase their rank for more power. Most Gnash live ordinary lives as civilians, and many leave the Demon Realm to live in the Human Realm behind Duskveil.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: 2 horns and 2 wings, small and stubby, barely more than bumps. Their wings are the smallest of all demon ranks, thin and often kept retracted. They look the most human out of all the ranks, which fits since they’re the ones taken to the Sundering Altar and still closest to an ordinary life before their power grows. Their aura is the weakest and gives an ominous feeling. Mauve, purple colored wings.

fields.label: Skills
fields.value: Binding Contract, Veyn Decomposition (Gnash), Instinctive Bargaining, Demonic Aura (Gnash), Duskveil (Gnash) — each skill has its own entry in the Angel Skills / Demon Skills categories.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Dregs

name: Duskveil
subtitle: The innate demonic disguise
description: Innate to all demons. Lets them blend into any society, hiding their true form and aura. The higher the rank, the more effective the disguise and the less power it costs to maintain; the lower the rank, the weaker the disguise and the more it cuts into their true strength.

fields.label: Mordrach
fields.value: Can pass flawlessly, even under scrutiny. Cuts their true strength by half while active.

fields.label: Bloodward
fields.value: Holds up well, though subtle tells (eyes, a shadow at the wrong angle) could give them away under close or magical scrutiny. Cuts their true strength by roughly 60%.

fields.label: Scourge
fields.value: Rougher and less convincing, more likely to slip under stress or in combat. Cuts their true strength by roughly 70%.

fields.label: Gnash
fields.value: The weakest version, thin enough to break under any real scrutiny. Cuts their true strength by roughly 80%, though since Gnash already look close to human naturally, they rely on it the least.

name: Humans
subtitle: The versatile race — affinity can change
description: Unlike other races, humans aren’t locked into one Veyn affinity for life. When an elf, angel, or demon is revealed at the altar, that affinity stays fixed forever, but a human’s affinity can change or grow over time through training. This means a human could eventually learn more than one affinity, something no other race can do. The catch is that switching or adding a new affinity is extremely hard. Most humans try and give up, choosing to stick with the one affinity they got at the altar instead. Even the ones who succeed never become as powerful in any single affinity as a race built specifically for it — they trade raw power for versatility. Humans can also learn all the skills of their chosen class, while other races are limited to 5.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Race - Dominant Population

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Most numerous race. Shortest lifespans (80-120 years) but most diverse class system. Adap fastest. Only race using all 18 classes. Weakness: no individual can match high-rank angel or demon.

name: Healers
subtitle: The seven healers of the Human Realm
description: There are only seven Healers in the Human Realm — and the seven Healers are the only seven holders of the Clergy class. When one of the seven dies, the Seer chooses the next Healer within two years, locating them through the Truthstone. To be a Healer is to hold the Clergy class; the two are one and the same.

fields.label: Role
fields.value: The seven Healers are the only seven Clergy class-holders in the world.

name: The Truthstone
subtitle: The gem that locates the next Healer
description: A gem entrusted to The Seer. It has the power to locate who the new Healer is. The Seer is the only one who knows the gem’s location.

fields.label: Keeper
fields.value: The Seer

name: Veyn
subtitle: The ambient magic of the world
description: It is what allows people to use magic in the world. It is drawn from the core of the world and everything around us. Veyn naturally glows a pale silver-blue, like faint moonlight. This is its raw, neutral form before it’s shaped into something else. Holy energy brightens it into gold, while corrupted Veyn (like a demon’s miasma) darkens it into deep purple or black.

fields.label: Feel
fields.value: Cool and ambient.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Drawn from the core of the world and everything around us.

fields.label: Color
fields.value: Naturally glows pale silver-blue like faint moonlight; holy energy brightens it into gold, while corrupted Veyn (like a demon’s miasma) darkens it into deep purple or black.

name: Holy Energy
subtitle: The purified form of Veyn
description: Holy energy is Veyn purified and brightened into gold — the form of Veyn channeled by angels, saints, diviners, paladins, and other holy beings. Where raw Veyn glows a neutral silver-blue, holy energy glows gold and burns corruption on contact, so it is naturally strong against undead, miasma, and corrupted Veyn while doing little to anything uncorrupted. It is not a separate source of power — it is Veyn refined, drawn from the same world core and bound by the same limits.

fields.label: Color
fields.value: Gold

fields.label: Nature
fields.value: Purified Veyn — not a separate source

fields.label: Used by
fields.value: Angels, saints, diviners, paladins, and other holy beings — including the angel half of the hybrid Jaiden Marlock.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Burns corruption on contact — strong against undead, miasma, and corrupted Veyn; weak against the uncorrupted

name: Corrupted Veyn
subtitle: The corrupted form of Veyn
description: Corrupted Veyn is Veyn darkened and corrupted into a deep purple or black — the form of Veyn that demons wield, which they call miasma. Where raw Veyn glows a neutral silver-blue and holy energy brightens it into gold, corrupted Veyn darkens it, poisoning and contaminating whatever it touches. It harms humans and can contaminate holy auras and holy energy. It is not a separate source of power — it is Veyn corrupted, drawn from the same world core and bound by the same limits.

fields.label: Color
fields.value: Deep purple or black

fields.label: Nature
fields.value: Corrupted Veyn — not a separate source

fields.label: Also called
fields.value: Miasma

fields.label: Used by
fields.value: Demons

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Harms humans and contaminates holy auras and holy energy

name: Ren
subtitle: The inner energy of swordsmen
description: It is what swordsmen use in place of Veyn. It is the inner energy from our body brought out to enhance our strength. Ren glows a deep crimson red since it is drawn from a person’s own Vitality rather than an outside source. Where Veyn feels cool and ambient, Ren feels warm and physical, more like a pulse than a light.

fields.label: Feel
fields.value: Warm and physical, like a pulse.

fields.label: Vitality
fields.value: Ren is drawn from a person’s own Vitality — their life energy.

name: Auric Ren
subtitle: The golden form of Ren
description: Auric Ren is Ren brightened into gold — a person’s own inner Vitality refined into a radiant, holy-tinged form, the way Holy Energy is Veyn purified. Where raw Ren glows a deep crimson, Auric Ren glows a warm white-gold, and instead of only strengthening the body it can heal and protect. Because it is still Ren — drawn from the body’s own Vitality rather than the world core — a paladin who wields Auric Ren never holds Veyn and Ren together, and so never suffers their incompatibility.

fields.label: Color
fields.value: Warm white-gold

fields.label: Nature
fields.value: Auric Ren — not a separate source

fields.label: Used by
fields.value: Paladins and other holy warriors

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Strengthens, heals, and protects using the body’s own gold-brightened Vitality

name: Concentrated Veyn
subtitle: Brighter, denser Veyn
description: Matches the color of a Lucent Stone: the same silver-blue as raw Veyn, just far brighter and more vivid, clear rather than faint or hazy.

fields.label: Color
fields.value: Same silver-blue as raw Veyn, just far brighter and more vivid — clear rather than faint or hazy.

name: Saturation Sickness
subtitle: The cost of lingering in concentrated Veyn
description: Caused by staying near or within concentrated Veyn for too long. The body can’t regulate the overwhelming amount of ambient Veyn, causing a person’s own Veyn to leak out constantly rather than being properly contained. This leaves them unable to perform any real magic (at most just basic spells), along with constant weakness, vomiting, and excessive sleep as the body struggles against the imbalance.

fields.label: Cause
fields.value: Staying near or within concentrated Veyn for too long.

fields.label: Symptoms
fields.value: Constant weakness, vomiting, and excessive sleep; unable to perform any real magic (at most basic spells) as the body leaks its own Veyn.

name: Corruption Sickness
subtitle: What corrupted Veyn does to a human
description: When a human comes into contact with corrupted Veyn, it does not kill them at once — it corrupts their own Veyn and slowly kills them over three stages, each worse than the last, like a disease eating through the body. Holy energy is the only thing that can halt or reverse it, and only in the early stages.

fields.label: Stage 1 — The Taint
fields.value: The corrupted Veyn darkens the Veyn at the point of contact. Symptoms: nausea, fatigue, and a faint grey-purple discoloration where it touched. Still reversible with holy energy.

fields.label: Stage 2 — The Spread
fields.value: The corruption spreads through the body's Veyn channels. Symptoms: constant pain, blackened veins surfacing under the skin, unstable or darkening magic, and rapid weakening. Only strong holy purification can halt it.

fields.label: Stage 3 — The End
fields.value: The corruption consumes the body's Veyn entirely, and the body fails as its own poisoned Veyn destroys it from within. Death is inevitable; holy energy can only ease the pain.

name: Affinity & Awakening
subtitle: How Veyn affinity is revealed and chosen
description:
At 15, every person is brought to the Sundering Altar where their latent connection to Veyn is unlocked — no one can consciously access magic before this. The altar doesn't teach them to use it; it simply opens the channel. The moment Veyn awakens, it manifests visibly in a way that reveals their affinity (combat-magic, healing, elemental control, beast-bonding, etc.) and their class — the specific discipline they are best suited for. The altar also determines their starting grade (how much latent Veyn they possess), which sets the foundation for their future growth. This is not a conscious choice in the moment; it is revealed based on what's already latent inside them. Path-choosing comes after: once someone knows their affinity and class, they choose how to pursue it (which order, mentor, discipline, or role to commit to).

Why the Academy matters: Awaken magic naturally is extremely difficult — even angels, who swear Veyn Vows to force their connection open, struggle with the process. Most humans and demons cannot awaken without help. The Sundering Altar was created by Kael von Ashen, the Headmaster of Elyndor Academy, using knowledge passed down from the Aelthar. The altar dramatically lowers the barrier to awakening, making it possible for ordinary people to access their Veyn. Because the altar is under the Academy's care, all children of every race — human, angel, demon, and beyond — are brought to Elyndor Academy at age 15 to undergo their awakening. The Academy provides the only reliable way for the world's people to develop magical abilities, which is why it holds such a central and respected position across all three realms.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: World Mechanic - Veyn Affinity

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Every being has natural Veyn affinity. Awakening is discovering/activating it. Determines learnable skills. Most humans have one affinity; hybrids have dual (Holy + Corrupted).

name: Class Skill Limits
subtitle: Humans can master a class fully; other races are capped
description: All races can use skills of their chosen class, but since the Angel and Demon realms have innate skills already, the max skills they can learn from their class is 5, while humans can learn all the skills of that class. Learning a skill from a class other than your own, however, is another matter: it is extremely difficult for humans to do, so hard that most never manage it, and they stick to what the altar gave them.

fields.label: Cross-class
fields.value: Learning skills from a class other than your own is extremely difficult for humans — most never manage it and stick to what the altar gave them.

name: Veyn & Ren Incompatibility
subtitle: You can never hold both
description: Joining magic and Bladesinger is not possible since Veyn and Ren are not compatible; you can’t have Ren and Veyn together in your body since it can kill you due to their extreme incompatibility. The one exception is Smithing — a Smith may draw on both during the forge, but can never learn any skill outside Smithing and the forging of weapons. Angels and demons can unlock a Ren Organ to channel Ren, but the same rule applies: while the organ is open they cannot touch any Veyn, or the incompatibility kills them.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: World Mechanic - Energy Conflict

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Holy Energy and Corrupted Veyn cannot coexist without a stabilizer. Using both causes Saturation Sickness. Only Hybrid form channels both without harm.

name: Growing Your Veyn Capacity
subtitle: How to increase your pool
description: The amount of Veyn someone can use from birth is already set. If you want to increase it, finish it (use it all up) and keep replenishing your Veyn for it to increase.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: World Mechanic - Training

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Veyn capacity increases through: 1) Veyn conditioning, 2) Grade advancement, 3) Rune Star Circles, 4) Mastered/Personalized skills.

name: Inheritance of Ranks & Abilities
subtitle: Not always passed down
description: A rank can be passed down to an offspring, though not all the time — otherwise they would have to work their way up the ranks. Abilities learnt can also be passed down to your offspring, though not all the time.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: World Mechanic - Lineage

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Angels/demons inherit rank potential from parents. Serapharch child can reach Serapharch. Gnash child limited to Scourge. Humans inherit class affinity but not grade.

name: The Hidden Realm Portal
subtitle: Moves every leap year
description: The portal to the Hidden Realm changes its location every leap year. It forms by drawing in all the Veyn from its surroundings until the area is fully drained, then uses what it absorbed to relocate itself somewhere new that’s rich in Veyn. The amount of time it takes for enough Veyn to concentrate in a new location happens to be roughly a leap year, which is why the portal only reappears that often. Since it’s drawn to wherever Veyn is rich rather than moving randomly, someone with a strong enough sense of Veyn density could theoretically predict roughly where it might appear next.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: World Mechanic - Realm Travel

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Portal moves every leap year. Opens with specific Veyn sequence. Time inside flows 10x slower. Opened only 3 times in recorded history.

name: Grade System
subtitle: The universal power scale
description: Every awakened being is measured by a Grade, from G (never exposed to Veyn) through F, E, D, C, B, A, to S (demigod). Grades run from level 0 to 100, each with Early, Mid, Late, and Peak sub-stages, a Wall at the peak of each grade, and an Evolution Quest to advance. Mages are the exception — they progress through Rune Star Circles instead.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: World Mechanic - Power Ranking

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Universal ranking: D (weakest) to C to B to A to S (strongest). Determined by Veyn capacity, skill mastery, combat effectiveness. Requires training and breakthrough.

name: G Grade
subtitle: Mortal Grade — Level 0-9
description: The starting grade assigned to beings who were never exposed to Veyn before gaining access to the System. This usually means those born in uninitiated worlds before integration. Any being born after System integration is assigned F Grade at minimum. G Grade beings have no sub-stages and cannot advance through normal means — they must first be exposed to Veyn.

fields.label: Sub-stages
fields.value: None

fields.label: Lifespan
fields.value: Normal human lifespan

name: F Grade
subtitle: First Grade — Level 10-19
description: The first true grade of the System. F Grade beings have been exposed to Veyn and can begin developing their abilities. This is the starting point for most awakened individuals. F Grade has no sub-stages — it is a transitional grade where the foundation is built before the real progression begins.

fields.label: Sub-stages
fields.value: None

fields.label: Note
fields.value: Foundation stage — no sub-stages

name: E Grade
subtitle: Evolution Grade — Level 20-29
description: The first major evolutionary step. E Grade represents a substantial increase in power, influence, and connection to the System. Beings at this grade can sense and manipulate Veyn or Ren with increasing skill. Advancing from E to D requires completing an Evolution Quest.

description: A significant power jump. D Grade beings can influence their surroundings on a larger scale and are considered competent fighters. Most adventurers and class-holders operate at this grade. The average lifespan extends to roughly 1,000 years.

subtitle: Behemoth Grade — Level 60-74
description: A grade of immense power. B Grade beings can destroy cities, manipulate large-scale Veyn flows, and are considered apex threats in most regions. The difference between B and C is vast — a single B Grade can wipe out an army of C Grades.

subtitle: Apex Grade — Level 75-89
description: The highest mortal grade. A Grade beings are forces of nature — they can reshape terrain, command armies, and rival the power of lesser divine beings. Few reach this grade; those who do are legends in their own time.

subtitle: Sovereign Grade — Level 90-100
description: The pinnacle of mortal power. S Grade beings are demigods — nearing godhood itself. Peak S Grade individuals are known as Demigods. The difference between S and A is the difference between a mortal and something beyond mortal comprehension.

name: The Wall
subtitle: Natural Barrier to Advancement
description: Every being reaches a wall — a natural barrier to the path beyond that they must overcome by any means possible. Failure will result in the stagnation of progress. Many beings resign themselves to their fates when this happens; others accept it and move on with the hope that they can progress once more in the future. The Wall appears at the peak of each grade and must be broken through to advance.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Blocks advancement until overcome

fields.label: Trigger
fields.value: Appears at the peak of each grade

fields.label: Failure
fields.value: Permanent stagnation at current grade

name: Evolution Quest
subtitle: Advancement Challenge
description: Upon reaching the peak of a grade, a being must complete an Evolution Quest to transition into the new grade. These quests vary in difficulty and nature — some require killing specific targets, others demand reaching certain milestones. Failing or not completing this quest restricts advancement. The difficulty of the quest scales with the grade being attempted.

fields.label: Trigger
fields.value: Reaching peak of current grade

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Unlocks next grade upon completion

fields.label: Failure
fields.value: Cannot advance until quest is completed

name: 1st Circle Rune Star
subtitle: Mage Circle 1 — Initiate
description: The first circle of the Rune Star system. A Mage at this circle has learned to inscribe basic Rune Stars — small sigils of condensed Veyn that serve as the foundation for all higher circles. Spells cast at this circle are simple but functional: bolts, shields, and basic elemental effects. The 1st Circle is where every Mage begins, and where most remain. The Veyn cost is low, but so is the power. The Rune Star is physically carved into the Mage's heart — each circle is a new sigil burned into the cardiac tissue by Veyn. The process is excruciatingly painful, as the heart is the most sensitive organ in the body and the Veyn must be channeled directly into living flesh. Upgrading is not optional once begun — a half-inscribed Rune Star will destabilize and kill the Mage. Each circle must be completed fully before the next can be attempted. Skipping circles is suicide: the backlash from an incomplete inscription tears through the heart and kills the Mage instantly. This is why Mages must progress step by step, one circle at a time, enduring the agony of each inscription knowing that hesitation or impatience means death.

Spells at this circle are noticeably stronger — a 1st Circle bolt becomes a 2nd Circle lance that pierces through armor. The Mage begins to feel the weight of Veyn flowing through two sigils instead of one. Each spell is not just stronger, but faster and more precise. The Rune Star is physically carved into the Mage's heart — each circle is a new sigil burned into the cardiac tissue by Veyn. Spells at this circle can shatter walls, summon storms, and create barriers that withstand siege-level attacks. The jump from 2nd to 3rd is the first truly dramatic leap — a 3rd Circle spell can overpower multiple 2nd Circle spells simultaneously. Spells at this circle can level city blocks, create illusions indistinguishable from reality, and manipulate the weather over entire regions. The power gap between 3rd and 4th is enormous — a single 4th Circle spell can annihilate an army of 3rd Circle Mages. name: 5th Circle Rune Star
subtitle: Mage Circle 5 — Archmage
description: The fifth circle. Five Rune Stars arranged in a pentagram create a Veyn matrix that resonates with the world core itself. At this circle, the Mage can touch the raw source of Veyn and draw upon it directly. Spells at this circle can reshape terrain, create pocket dimensions, and strike with the force of natural disasters. The jump from 4th to 5th is the most dramatic — a 5th Circle Mage is no longer a person who uses magic, but a person who IS magic. Only a handful exist in any generation. The Rune Star is physically carved into the Mage's heart — each circle is a new sigil burned into the cardiac tissue by Veyn. The process is excruciatingly painful, as the heart is the most sensitive organ in the body and the Veyn must be channeled directly into living flesh. Upgrading is not optional once begun — a half-inscribed Rune Star will destabilize and kill the Mage. Each circle must be completed fully before the next can be attempted. Skipping circles is suicide: the backlash from an incomplete inscription tears through the heart and kills the Mage instantly. This is why Mages must progress step by step, one circle at a time, enduring the agony of each inscription knowing that hesitation or impatience means death.

name: The Two Sundering Altars
subtitle: Common Altar and Academy Altar
description:
There are two Sundering Altars in the world, each serving a different purpose. The Common Altar is located in a neutral temple between the three realms and is where most ordinary people go for their awakening at age 15. The Academy Altar is located within Elyndor Academy and is reserved for students accepted into the Academy. The Academy Altar is significantly more powerful — it provides a clearer reading of a person's class affinity and starting grade, and can handle a wider range of race types including angels and demons. Both altars were built by Kael von Ashen using Aelthar knowledge, but the Academy Altar was constructed with additional materials recovered from the Hidden Realm, making it far more precise.

The Common Altar can only reveal a person's general affinity (combat, healing, support, etc.) and a rough estimate of their grade. The Academy Altar can pinpoint the exact class a person is suited for (Mage, Alchemist, Paladin, etc.), determine their precise starting grade, and even detect innate abilities or unusual Veyn signatures. This is why the Academy accepts students from all three realms — even angels and demons send their children to Elyndor for the awakening, despite the political tensions between the realms. The Academy's neutrality in this matter is one of the reasons it has survived for so long.

name: The Rune Star System
subtitle: How Mages inscribe and upgrade their Rune Stars
description:
The Rune Star is the foundation of all Mage power. Unlike other classes that develop their abilities through training and experience, Mages must physically inscribe Rune Star sigils into their heart. Each circle is a new sigil burned directly into the cardiac tissue by Veyn — the most sensitive organ in the body. The inscription process is excruciatingly painful, as the Veyn must be channeled into living flesh without killing the Mage. This is why Mages are rare and their progression is slow: the pain is so severe that many abandon the path after their first circle, and those who continue must have extraordinary willpower and pain tolerance.

The rules of the Rune Star system are absolute: each circle must be fully completed before the next can be attempted. A half-inscribed Rune Star will destabilize and kill the Mage. Skipping circles is instant death — the backlash from an incomplete inscription tears through the heart and destroys it. There are no shortcuts, no exceptions. A Mage who attempts to jump from 2nd Circle to 4th Circle, for example, will die before the 4th sigil is even begun. This is why Mages must progress step by step, one circle at a time, enduring the agony of each inscription.

The 7th Circle Rune Star cannot be inscribed by the Mage themselves — it must be given by the world core. Only one being in recorded history has received this gift, and the world was forever changed by it.

It’s used in stronger brews and enchantments where a regular Veyn Stone wouldn’t be enough; a single Lucent Stone can be worth several raw Veyn Stones combined. fields.label: Description
fields.value: Massive ancient trees in the Hidden Realm. Bark is impervious to normal weapons. Wood carves into Corrupted Veyn weapons. Semi-sentient and hostile to intruders.

name: Ebonspire Tree
subtitle: The 100-year tree of dragon nests
description: It is found and grows near the nest of a dragon. It is a 100-year-old tree. The leaves can be used to make an elixir named the Rejuvenating Elixir, while the bark when grinded to powder can be used in making the Ethereal Potion.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Hidden Realm - Ancient Flora

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Towering obsidian-colored trees in the deepest Hidden Realm. Sap is a potent healing agent. Grow in patterns forming natural labyrinths.

name: Ethereal Potion
subtitle: Legendary-rank elixir that halts aging
description: A legendary-rank elixir, difficult to brew correctly — a single miscalculation wastes the rare ingredients entirely. Rather than restoring or boosting Veyn or Ren, it halts the drinker’s aging completely for a long, fixed stretch of time rather than reversing it like pixie dust does.

fields.label: Ingredients
fields.value: Pixie dust, grinded leaves of the Grimbough tree, grinded powder from the bark of the Ebonspire tree, the heart of a dragon

name: Rejuvenating Elixir
subtitle: Complete healing
description: A potion that does a complete heal of the person who drinks it. Can even heal broken legs or lost arms. The version found in the vault of Lethmoor can heal the impossible, except a severed head or a missing heart past 10 minutes.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Hidden Realm - Consumable

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Legendary potion from Hidden Realm ingredients. Heals any wound except decapitation. Full HP restore and removes all negative effects. Priceless.

name: Vireth, the Fallen Grace
subtitle: The corrupted divine sword sealed in the Sentient River
description: Sealed within the depths of the Sentient River, held down by two separate seals rather than one, as though whoever bound it there didn’t trust a single ward to be enough. The blade itself is dark, almost absorbing the light around it rather than reflecting it, with faint cracks of dim gold light bleeding through along the fuller — like the last remnants of what it used to be before it fell. Even sealed, the water around it never fully settles; the current near it moves like something is still restless beneath the surface. Strangely, the blade doesn’t feel like something purely angelic or purely demonic — whatever corruption twisted it seems to have left behind a blade that belongs fully to neither side. Very effective against an angel or a demon; it can stop the regeneration of both races effectively unless the user releases the effect. A user bound weapon. One of the only ways to kill a Serapharch.

fields.label: Skill — Graceless Edge
fields.value: Cuts through both holy wards and demonic wards equally, treating corrupted and uncorrupted Veyn as the same thing to sever — essentially cutting magic if you have enough Veyn to cut it.

fields.label: Skill — Split Grace
fields.value: Channels both a holy (angelic) and a corrupted (demonic) aura through the blade at the same time, striking with both auras layered into one attack. Dangerous to hold even briefly; causes a force-splitting explosion of the cut area.

fields.label: Location
fields.value: Depths of the Sentient River, under two seals

fields.label: User-bound
fields.value: Binds to the user’s soul — anyone else who tries to use it finds it becomes nothing more than a piece of metal.

name: Virastra, the Ascendant Vow
subtitle: The uncorrupted divine sword, lost in the ruins
description: Lost somewhere in the ruins scattered across the Hidden Realm, no longer in anyone’s possession. Unlike Vireth, its blade is untouched, still holding a clean, steady light along its edge — closer to moonlight than sunlight. Where Vireth feels heavy and restless, Virastra is said to feel almost weightless in the hand, an ease that reflects its uncorrupted nature. Being lost among ruins rather than deliberately sealed, its exact location isn’t guarded the way Vireth’s is — it’s simply forgotten, waiting for someone to stumble upon it rather than seek it out. Extremely effective against demons and halts a demon’s regeneration unless the user releases the effect.

fields.label: Weapon type
fields.value: Divine Sword

fields.label: Location
fields.value: Lost somewhere in the ruins scattered across the Hidden Realm

name: Solvane, the Hallowed Edge
subtitle: The divine spear still in someone’s possession
description: The only one of the two Divine Weapons still in someone’s possession rather than lost or sealed away. Unlike Vireth’s restless darkness or Virastra’s weightless calm, Solvane carries itself with quiet authority — its head long and narrow, more piercing than cutting, forged for a single decisive strike rather than a prolonged exchange. The metal holds a steady, clean light along its edge, similar in tone to Virastra’s, since neither has ever been corrupted — but where Virastra’s light feels ambient and calm, Solvane’s feels focused, almost gathered to a point, fitting a weapon built to be thrown or thrust with precision rather than swung. Will always return to the owner when thrown. A user bound weapon that can be passed down.

fields.label: Weapon type
fields.value: Divine Spear

fields.label: Owner
fields.value: Clint Ashborn — the current ruler of the Angel Realm.

fields.label: Notable
fields.value: Always returns to the owner when thrown; user bound weapon that can be passed down.

fields.label: User-bound
fields.value: Binds to the user’s soul — anyone else who tries to use it finds it becomes nothing more than a piece of metal.

name: Aerendrel, the Skybound Wrath
subtitle: The storm-strung bow of the Lethmoor vault
description: A unique divine-adjacent bow, said to have been strung with a fragment of storm itself rather than ordinary sinew or Veyn. Those loosed from it don’t just pierce — they carry a violent surge of raw elemental force (lightning, wind, or pressure), which detonates on impact rather than simply striking true. Unlike a standard Archer’s Veyn-enchanted arrows, which are shaped and controlled, Aerendrel’s power is closer to a contained storm — difficult to fully master, and even harder to wield without some of that raw force spilling back onto the archer themselves. It doesn’t need arrows: the bow forms arrows from the user’s Veyn. Found in the chamber beneath Lethmoor’s throne chair.

fields.label: Location
fields.value: Vault of Lethmoor Kingdom (chamber beneath the throne chair)

fields.label: Note
fields.value: "Sinew" refers to a tendon — the tough, fibrous connective tissue that attaches muscle to bone.

name: Liework’s Fallen Crown
subtitle: The decayed crown of a fallen kingdom
description: Shaped like a twisted ring of black thorned vines rather than a traditional band of gold — more a wreath of dead growth than a symbol of triumph. Wherever the true crown once looked like, this is what remained after the kingdom fell: thorns in place of jewels, black in place of gleaming metal, as if the crown itself decayed alongside the throne it once sat on. Wearing it doesn’t grant strength so much as command — faint traces of the authority its last wearer held still cling to it, enough to lean on an Angelic Aura-style effect, making those weaker than the wearer more inclined to submit, though nowhere near as absolute as a true Serapharch’s presence.

fields.label: Location
fields.value: Vault of Lethmoor Kingdom

name: Selene’s Luck
subtitle: One critical strike, blocked
description: A luck pendant that blocks a critical/fatal strike that can kill you once, and then breaks.

fields.label: Location
fields.value: Vault of Lethmoor Kingdom

name: Auralis Ruby
subtitle: The pendant that sealed the MC’s forms
description: A pendant crafted by the MC’s mom (Lisa), who then gave it to Sofia. The pendant has 5 seals to seal the MC’s 5 forms, and the seals are not equal — each seal is stronger than the one before it, so the 1st seal is the weakest and the 5th is the strongest. It seals both of his auras (angelic and demonic), which makes him look human. When a seal breaks, the strain it was holding does not vanish — it passes to the next seal. If that next seal is pushed past its own limit, it will break or weaken in turn. A broken seal can mend over time, but never back to full strength, and a weakened seal cracks more easily the next time it is tested.

fields.label: Crafted by
fields.value: Lisa, a Bloodward demon

fields.label: Keeper
fields.value: Sofia

fields.label: Seal Strength
fields.value: The 5 seals escalate in strength — 1st is weakest, 5th is strongest. Each is stronger than the one before it.

fields.label: Break Chain
fields.value: When a seal breaks, its strain passes to the next seal; if that seal is pushed past its limit, it breaks or weakens too.

fields.label: Recovery
fields.value: A broken seal mends over time, but never to full strength — and a weakened seal breaks more easily afterward.

name: Agro Totem
subtitle: Summon a storm of monsters
description: A totem made to attract a storm of monsters to it, make all the monsters angry, and boost the power of monsters by 10. For it to work, 2 must be made: the first is set in the monster area, and the other at the desired location — when you infuse Veyn once into the second totem at the designed location, the monsters are drawn there. It can be crafted with blood of a siren, a Lucent Stone, blood of a Veilborn, and a hay doll on a stick.

fields.label: Ingredients
fields.value: Blood of a siren, Lucent Stone, blood of a Veilborn, a hay doll on a stick

name: Jaiden Marlock
subtitle: The first Angel-Demon Hybrid — protagonist of the Half-Made World
description:
Jaiden Marlock is the first Angel-Demon Hybrid in the world's history — a being that should not exist, born of two races whose natures are fundamentally opposed. His father, Ordium, was an Aetherblade Lord Angel and the First Pillar of the Six Pillars. His mother, Lisa, was a Bloodward demon, the most powerful demon in the Demon Realm after the Mordrach. Their love was forbidden by every law, every vow, and every pact in existence. When Lisa discovered she was pregnant, she knew the child would be killed — both realms would see an angel-demon hybrid as an abomination. She gave the child to her personal maid, Sofia, along with the Auralis Ruby pendant to seal his auras. Sofia fled to the Human Realm, and Jaiden grew up in a small house, believing himself to be ordinary.

He is not ordinary. He is the subject of the Prophecy of the Half-Made — the being who will stand at the fourth turning of the Sundering Prophecy Cycle and choose "the seam or the silence." Every faction in the world has a plan for him: Clint Ashborn wants him controlled or destroyed, Tera Morage wants him dead, Ruby Divina wants him as humanity's leverage, Wener Leger wants him as a weapon, and Kael von Ashen wants to show him the truth.

Jaiden does not know any of this when the story begins. He is a boy of fifteen, living with Sofia, whose awakening at the Sundering Altar has already happened — and gone wrong. He knows he is different — the Auralis Ruby hides his true form, and sometimes the seals strain — but he does not know why. The story is about him learning what he is, deciding what it means, and choosing what to do with it.

---

APPEARANCE

Normal Form (sealed by Auralis Ruby):
Jaiden looks fully human — no wings, no horns, no halo. He is a lean, sharp-featured young man of about 15, with dark hair that falls past his ears and grey eyes that occasionally flicker with an inner light he cannot explain. He is of average height but carries himself like someone used to being watched, shoulders slightly hunched, eyes always moving. His most distinctive feature is the Auralis Ruby pendant at his throat — a deep red stone that pulses faintly with a light only he can feel. When the seals strain, the ruby grows warm and his veins glow faintly beneath his skin, alternating between gold (angelic) and violet (demonic).

True Form (when seals release):
In his full hybrid form, he is something no one has ever seen: 3 pure white feathery wings on one half of his body, 3 black feathery wings on the other, 6 horns curling from his forehead, and a halo split in half floating above his head — one half golden and bright, the other half dark and cracked. Both the angelic and demonic auras surround him simultaneously, creating a pressure that makes the air feel heavy. His eyes become heterochromatic: one gold, one violet.

---

PERSONALITY

Core Traits:
  • Curious — Jaiden asks questions constantly. He wants to understand how things work, why people do what they do, and what he is. This curiosity is his greatest strength and his greatest danger — it leads him to truths that others would prefer stayed hidden.
  • Stubborn — Once Jaiden decides something matters, he does not let go. This makes him resilient in the face of overwhelming odds but also prone to tunnel vision when he should be adapting.
  • Compassionate — He cares about people, even people who have no reason to care about him. This is partly nature (his angel half) and partly upbringing (Sofia raised him to be kind). It is also his greatest vulnerability — caring about people gives the world leverage over him.
  • Self-doubting — Jaiden does not trust his own judgment. He has spent his life being told he is different, hiding his true nature, and relying on others to keep him safe. When the weight of decision falls on him, he hesitates. The story is about him learning to trust himself.
  • Dry humor — Jaiden copes with fear and confusion through sarcasm. He is not a jokester; his humor is quiet, observational, and often self-deprecating. It is a defense mechanism, and people who know him well can tell when he is afraid by how sharp his wit becomes.

How Others See Him:
  • Sofia: The child she raised. She sees the boy he was, not the weapon others want him to be. She is fiercely protective and terrified of the day she cannot protect him anymore.
  • Bella Rose: His childhood friend. She sees someone who has always been quietly extraordinary — someone who helps without being asked and disappears when the attention gets too heavy. She does not know his secret, but she knows he is hiding something.
  • Mark Wesley: His loyal friend. Mark sees Jaiden as the person who made him feel like he belonged at the Academy. Mark is uncomplicated and warm, and his friendship is one of the few things that makes Jaiden feel normal.
  • Carin: His demonic trainer. She sees Lisa in him — the same stubbornness, the same quiet fury — and it both comforts and frightens her. She pushes him hard because she knows the world will push harder.
  • Kael von Ashen: The last Aelthar sees in Jaiden the possibility that the Sundering can be healed — or the certainty that it will be completed. He treats Jaiden with a mixture of hope and caution that Jaiden finds unsettling.
  • Clint Ashborn: The Serapharch sees a threat to everything he has built. Jaiden's existence is proof that the Angel Realm's laws are incomplete, and Clint does not tolerate incompleteness.
  • Ruby Divina: The mortal ruler sees a card to play. She shields Jaiden not from kindness but because he is humanity's insurance policy. She respects him but does not love him — yet.
  • Wener Leger: The fallen angel sees a weapon. Jaiden's hybrid nature makes him the most dangerous being in the world, and Wener wants to control that danger.

---

INTERNAL CONFLICTS

1. Identity: "What am I?"
Jaiden is neither angel nor demon nor human. He is all three and none of them. Every culture in the world has a place for its people — angels have the Vow, demons have the Pact, humans have the Faith — but Jaiden has no category. He cannot take the Vow (no single promise binds both natures), he cannot make a Pact (demons would reject him as an abomination), and the World Core Faith does not account for beings like him. He must build his own identity from scratch, which is terrifying when you are 15 and the world already wants to define you.

2. Belonging: "Where do I fit?"
Jaiden has spent his life hiding. The Auralis Ruby seals his true form, making him look human. He has friends at the Academy — Bella, Mark, Eva — but they do not know what he is. Every relationship he has is built on a lie of omission. When the truth comes out, some people will stand by him. Others will not. The fear of losing the people he loves keeps him hiding, but hiding keeps him from being truly known.

3. Power: "What can I do with this?"
Jaiden has more Veyn than any angel or demon his age. He can draw on both holy energy and corrupted Veyn. He can enter forms that no one has ever seen. But power without control is destruction. Every time he releases a seal, the strain passes to the next one. Every time he fights, he risks breaking the Auralis Ruby entirely — and if all five seals break at once, his full hybrid form will manifest whether he wants it to or not. He must learn to control what he is before it controls him.

4. Legacy: "What did my parents do?"
Jaiden's parents are dead. Lisa was killed by Licent Varak's men. Ordium was executed by Clint Ashborn's order. They died for loving each other and for creating him. Jaiden carries their legacy — and their enemies. Licent Varak wants him dead because he is proof of Lisa's "crime." Clint Ashborn wants him controlled because he is proof that the Angel Realm's laws are incomplete. Jaiden must decide whether to honor his parents by living quietly or by changing the world they died in.

5. The Prophecy: "Do I have a choice?"
The Prophecy of the Half-Made says he will face a choice: "the seam or the silence." Every faction interprets this differently, and every faction wants to influence his decision. But what if the prophecy is wrong? What if the missing fragments change everything? What if the choice is not between mending and destroying, but between two kinds of destruction? Jaiden must decide whether to trust a prophecy written in a language no one can fully read — or to trust himself.

---

CHARACTER ARC

Act 1 — The Sealed Boy (Beginning)
Jaiden lives with Sofia in the Human Realm. He is fifteen. His awakening at the Sundering Altar has already happened, and it stuttered — two auras where there should have been one. He does not yet understand what he is. The Auralis Ruby keeps his seals intact, but it cracked at the altar, and the crack is still mending. He has always known he is different. The seals sometimes strain. The ruby sometimes grows warm. He has never told anyone.

Inciting Incident: At the Academy awakening, the Altar reacts to Jaiden unlike any other student. The Veyn signature it reads is impossible — two conflicting auras, one angelic, one demonic, in the same body. The Altar does not crash, but it stutters. Kael von Ashen, who is watching, goes very still. Bella Rose, standing nearby, feels her own Veyn surge in response — the reflexive surge from the world core, triggered by Jaiden's presence. Something has begun.

Act 2 — The Unraveling (Middle)
Jaiden enters the Academy. He befriends Bella Rose, Mark Wesley, and Eva Aldermere Divina. He trains in his Mage class. He struggles with the fact that his Veyn feels wrong — too much of it, too volatile, as though two competing forces are fighting inside him. The seals on the Auralis Ruby begin to strain. He discovers he can release the first seal temporarily, revealing his halo and two horns — the "Halo & Horns" form. The Academy notices. Kael von Ashen takes him aside and tells him the truth about his parentage. Jaiden learns he is the son of Ordium and Lisa, that both are dead, and that he is the subject of an ancient prophecy.

Midpoint Shift: Wener Leger, posing as a swordsmanship teacher, reveals himself to Jaiden as a fallen angel — and tells him that Dark Moon knows what he is. Licent Varak has sent agents to the Academy. The ticking clock begins: Jaiden must master his forms before the fourth turning, because if he cannot control his power, someone else will control it for him.

Act 3 — The Choice (Endgame)
The fourth turning of the Sundering Prophecy Cycle arrives. The World Eater stirs. The Abyssal Wyrm's seal weakens. The Shudon begin to show signs of reactivation. Every faction mobilizes. Jaiden must decide: does he use his power to mend the Sundering (stitching the realms back together, restoring the Aelthar's work, but potentially destroying the independence of every realm) or does he let the silence fall (allowing the World Eater to drain the Core, ending magic but preserving the current order)?

The answer is neither. Jaiden realizes the prophecy's missing fragments hold the key — the choice was never between mending and silence, but between two kinds of mending. He can heal the Sundering without destroying what grew from it. He can restore the connection between realms without erasing their differences. But the cost is everything he is — the hybrid nature, the dual auras, the power that makes him unique. He must give up what makes him special to save the world.

Resolution: Jaiden chooses to sacrifice his hybrid nature — not his life, but his dual auras — to mend the Sundering on his own terms. The Auralis Ruby shatters. His wings, horns, and halo fade. He becomes something new: not angel, not demon, not human, but the bridge between them. He cannot take the Vow because he no longer has the nature to support it. He cannot make a Pact because he no longer has the power to bind one. He is, finally and completely, himself — a person, not a prophecy.

The world does not end. The realms do not merge. The Sundering is not reversed — it is healed, the way a broken bone heals: stronger at the joint, weaker at the break, forever marked by what happened. And Jaiden Marlock, the first and last Hybrid, walks into a world that finally has a place for him — not as a weapon, not as a prophecy, but as a person who chose to be more than what he was made to be.

---

RELATIONSHIPS

Sofia Marlock (Guardian):
The woman who raised him. Jaiden loves Sofia more than anyone in the world. She is the only person who has always known what he is and loved him anyway. When the truth comes out, Sofia is the person he turns to first. She cannot protect him anymore — the world is too big, the enemies too powerful — but she can remind him of who he was before the prophecy, and that is enough to keep him grounded.

Bella Rose (Childhood Friend / Love Interest):
Jaiden has been in love with Bella since he was old enough to understand what love was. She does not know his secret, and the fear of her rejection keeps him at arm's length. When she learns the truth, their friendship fractures — not because she hates what he is, but because she hates that he hid it from her. Their relationship rebuilds slowly, forged in the fire of the fourth turning, and becomes something stronger than friendship but different from what Jaiden imagined.

Mark Wesley (Best Friend):
Mark is the person who makes Jaiden feel normal. He is warm, loyal, and uncomplicated — everything Jaiden is not. When Mark learns the truth, he does not hesitate: "You're still my friend. I don't care what you are." This simple acceptance is one of the most important moments in Jaiden's arc.

Kael von Ashen (Mentor):
The last Aelthar is the closest thing Jaiden has to a father figure — and the most complicated. Kael teaches Jaiden about his heritage, the Hidden Realm, and the Aelthar's legacy. But Kael also has his own agenda: he wants the Sundering healed, and he is willing to use Jaiden to do it. Jaiden must learn to trust Kael's wisdom without surrendering his own judgment.

Carin (Demonic Trainer):
Carin trained Lisa, and now she trains Jaiden. She pushes him hard because she knows what the world will do to someone who is not prepared. She does not coddle him, and Jaiden resents her for it — until he realizes she is the only person teaching him the truth about his demonic half without romanticizing it.

Eva Aldermere Divina (Ally):
Ruby Divina's daughter, attending the Academy on her mother's orders. Eva is political, ambitious, and genuinely kind — a combination that Jaiden finds confusing. She becomes his ally because her mother told her to, but she stays his ally because she believes in what he could become.

Licent Varak (Enemy):
The man who killed Jaiden's mother. Licent does not hate Jaiden personally — he hates what Jaiden represents: proof that Lisa's "crime" produced something powerful, something that validates everything Licent fought to destroy. Licent wants Jaiden dead because Jaiden's existence makes his betrayal of Lisa look like a mistake.

Clint Ashborn (Antagonist):
The Serapharch ordered Ordium's execution and has spent years trying to ensure no hybrid ever exists. Jaiden is proof that Clint's order failed. Clint does not hate Jaiden — he fears him. A being that carries both Vow and Pact is a theological crisis for the Angel Realm, and Clint will do anything to contain that crisis.

Wener Leger (Manipulator):
The fallen angel sees Jaiden as the ultimate weapon — a being who can wield both holy and demonic energy. Wener wants to control Jaiden, not kill him. His manipulation is subtle: he tells Jaiden truths that lead to the conclusions Wener wants. The hardest part for Jaiden is that Wener is not entirely wrong — the world IS unfair, the realms ARE broken, and the prophecy IS ambiguous. Jaiden must learn to distinguish between truth and manipulation.

Tera Morage (Threat):
The Mordrach wants Jaiden dead because he is an abomination — a being that carries both Vow and Pact in one body. Tera sees him as a threat to the natural order that demons depend on. She will send her generals to kill him before the fourth turning.

Ruby Divina (Protector / User):
The mortal ruler shields Jaiden because he is humanity's leverage. She does not love him — she respects him. When the time comes, she will ask him to choose humanity's interests over his own. Whether he does depends on how much she has earned his trust.

---

ABILITIES & LIMITATIONS

Class: Mage
Rune Star Circle: 3rd Circle
Power Level: Artificer
Inherited Skills: Auralis Seal, The Stolen Hour

What he can do:
  • Channel both Holy Energy (angelic) and Corrupted Veyn (demonic) — something no other being can do
  • Enter 5 distinct forms (sealed by the Auralis Ruby)
  • In True Hybrid Form, his skills fuse — each Aetherblade Lord skill and each Bloodward skill merge into a single hybrid skill
  • His Veyn reserves are abnormally large — more than any angel or demon his age
  • He can sense both holy and corrupted Veyn, giving him awareness that others lack

What he cannot do:
  • Take the Veyn Vow — no single promise binds both natures
  • Make a Demon Pact — demons would reject him as an abomination
  • Fully control his forms — each seal release strains the Auralis Ruby
  • Mix Veyn and Ren — the incompatibility rule would kill him
  • Trust his own power — every time he uses it, he risks losing control

The Auralis Ruby:
  • 5 seals, escalating in strength
  • 1st seal: weakest, can be released temporarily (Halo & Horns form)
  • 2nd seal: stronger (Full Angel Form)
  • 3rd seal: stronger still (Full Demon Form)
  • 4th seal: very strong (partial hybrid)
  • 5th seal: the strongest, holding back his full True Hybrid Form
  • When a seal breaks, strain passes to the next
  • Broken seals mend over time but never to full strength
  • If all 5 seals break at once, Jaiden manifests his full form whether he wants to or not

fields.value: Marlock is Sofia Marlock surname — Jaiden uses it as his public identity. His biological parents are Lisa and Ordium (no surname). Sofia took him in and gave him her name to protect him from those hunting hybrids.

name: Lisa
subtitle: Bloodward demon — most powerful after the Mordrach
description: She had a child for Ordium, and due to their ranks and positions they could not stay together and were separated to their various Realms: Lisa went to her realm, the Demon Realm, and Ordium went to the Angel Realm. Her rank was Bloodward. She was known to bring cruelty upon people who fight her and is the most powerful demon in the Demon Realm after the Mordrach. After realizing she was pregnant with Jaiden and found his aura very abnormal — carrying both an angelic aura and a demonic aura — she knew he would be killed off and she could not bear it, so she gave the child to her personal maid, not before giving her a ruby pendant called the Auralis Ruby to seal all his auras, which makes him look human.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: Six horns and six dark purple feathery wings. The horns are sharp and jagged, some cracked from old battles. Her wings are broad and scarred, carrying the marks of a commander who has fought at the front. She carries herself with quiet, dangerous poise.

fields.label: Rank
fields.value: Bloodward

fields.label: Fate
fields.value: Demoted to Gnash rank and killed by Licent Varak’s men after he reported her relationship with an angel.

description: The First Pillar — the highest-ranked of the six angel generals, the one the others took their orders from. He met Lisa and left his post for nine months. When the rulers called him back, they ordered him executed for lying with a demon. The First Pillar fell, and the five beneath him were never the same after.

fields.label: Appearance

name: Licent Varak
subtitle: Second right-hand man to Tera Morage — the betrayer
description: He is the second right-hand man to Tera Morage in the Demon Realm. He had always hated Lisa for being stronger than him and holding the top Bloodward position, so he was constantly looking for a way to take her power and rank away. When he saw Sofia heading to an unknown location, he tried to follow her but lost track of her. He then saw Lisa meet with an angel. After that, he discovered they had intercourse and that she had become pregnant with a child. He used this information to report her to Tera Morage, which enraged the ruler. As a result, Lisa was demoted to Gnash rank and later killed by his men, which he ordered them to do.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: Six horns and six dark purple feathery wings. His horns are sharp and jagged, his wings broad and scarred from battle. He carries himself with the tight, controlled posture of a soldier who is always measuring the distance between himself and the person above him.

name: Ruby Divina
subtitle: Ruler of the Human Realm (Female)
description: Ruby Divina is the only mortal ruler in a world governed by immortals — Clint Ashborn does not age, and Tera Morage dies of nothing short of a Divine Weapon, while Ruby will be gone within a mortal lifetime and knows it. She rules humanity, the one people with no wings, no halo, no miasma — just raw Veyn and short years — caught between two realms that could crush hers on a whim. Her whole reign has been the slow, careful work of making humanity too useful and too dangerous to be worth crushing. She has known about Jaiden Marlock from the beginning — the hybrid child hiding in her realm under a maid’s care is no secret to her — and she has shielded him not from kindness but because he is her insurance: a being both realms would go to war over, the one card that could make humanity a power instead of a client.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: A mortal woman of middling years with no wings, no horns, and no halo, purely human. She has the bearing of someone who learned to command rooms she was never supposed to enter, and the careful stillness of someone who knows her years are numbered.

fields.label: Grade
fields.value: B Grade

name: Tera Morage
subtitle: Ruler of the Demon Realm — Mordrach (Female)
description: Tera Morage did not inherit the Mordrach’s crown — she tore it from the king before her, the way every Fiend who ever ruled the Demon Realm rose by killing the one above, and she has never once relaxed her grip since. Unkillable by anything short of a Divine Weapon, she let that invulnerability curdle into contempt, ruling her generals and her right-hand men with the certainty that nothing in the realm can touch her. The single exception was Lisa. Lisa was not merely her right-hand — she was her friend, the one demon Tera trusted enough to keep close — and so when Licent Varak brought her the truth of Lisa’s affair with an angel, Tera did what no Mordrach is supposed to do: she showed mercy. She demoted Lisa to Gnash, a punishment meant to hurt but not to kill, because in a realm where strength is the only truth, that was the softest sentence she could pass without appearing weak. It was still a death sentence. Licent, who had only ever hated Lisa, had her killed by his own men — and Tera, who can be killed by nothing in her realm, learned that the one law she cannot bend is the one that put her on the throne: when a Mordrach dies, all the Veyn she holds passes to the heir who can withstand it. Her court is a circle of knives, every one of them waiting for a Divine Weapon to appear, and Licent Varak, her own second right-hand, is already in the dark with Dark Moon. She does not see it, because she has spent so long fearing nothing that she has forgotten how to fear her own shadow.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: Eight horns and eight deep-purple feathery wings. The horns curl back and are fused together at the base like a crown, massive and tattered at the edges but still powerful. Her dark feathers seem to absorb light rather than reflect it, and she carries the strongest demonic aura among all the demons.

fields.value: Mordrach

name: Clint Ashborn
subtitle: Ruler of the Angel Realm — Serapharch (Male)
description: Clint Ashborn has ruled the Angel Realm so long the realm has forgotten there was ever another way. He ordered his own right-hand man, Ordium, executed for loving a demon and fathering the hybrid child — and to Clint that was not cruelty but necessity, the one clean cut that kept chaos from the door. He believes the angels’ promises — the Veyn Vows each of them swore — and the order those promises uphold are the only things standing between peace and the collapse of everything, and he administers that belief with the serenity of a man who has never once doubted he was saving the world. He knows the buried truth of the world core’s will, and it frightens him more than any demon, because a will greater than the angelic order would mean the order he has upheld his whole existence is not the highest thing there is. Every impossible thing Jaiden Marlock is, is a refutation of Clint’s entire life — which is what makes him so dangerous an enemy: he is not wrong that the hybrid threatens the world’s balance, only wrong about what to do with it.

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: Eight large wings that almost cover his entire body, feathers glowing pale gold. His halo is a solid ring of light too bright to look at directly. He carries the strongest angelic aura among all the angels, an overwhelming presence that presses down on anyone nearby.
