fields.value: Coats the blade in poison. Next 3 attacks deal poison damage (3% max HP per second for 10 seconds).

name: Lock Touch
subtitle: Veilrunner skill
description: Uses Ren to sense and manipulate the internal mechanisms of locks without physical tools. At its most basic, the touch can pick simple mechanical locks. Complex magical locks require deeper concentration.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Touches a locked object, unlocking it instantly. Also works on magical locks.

name: Face Shift
subtitle: Veilrunner skill
description: Subtly alters posture, gait, and mannerisms to blend into crowds or imitate another person. At its most basic, the shift provides a general resemblance — not a perfect copy. The user can fool casual observation.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Changes appearance to match a target. Lasts 10 minutes or until the Shadow Blade attacks.

name: Disappear
subtitle: Veilrunner skill
description: Fully suppresses presence for a short time, becoming effectively invisible. At its most basic, the vanish lasts only a few seconds and movement is limited. The user's Veyn signature fades to nothing.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Becomes completely invisible for 8 seconds. Attacking or using skills breaks invisibility.

name: Living Shadow
subtitle: Veilrunner skill
description: Allows near-perfect stealth even at full speed, leaving almost no trace of the user's presence. At its most basic, the shadow provides near-invisible movement at walking speed. Faster movement may leave brief visual disturbances.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: The Shadow Blade’s shadow moves independently, scouting ahead and attacking enemies.

name: Stone Study
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Deep analysis of Shudon construction, materials, design, and age through examination. At its most basic, the study can identify the age and general origin of a Shudon fragment. The analysis requires physical contact and focused Veyn probing.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Reads the history of any stone or mineral object. Reveals its age, origin, and previous owners.

name: Stone Keep
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Repairs and maintains inactive Shudon, slowing further deterioration even if reactivation is impossible. At its most basic, the keep can patch cracks, clean surfaces, and reinforce fragile sections. The work is slow and meticulous.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Creates a small stone structure that provides shelter and +20% Veyn regeneration for 1 hour.

name: Golem Lore
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Theoretical knowledge of how the Shudon were originally created and what role the world core played. At its most basic, the lore covers the basic history and construction methods. The knowledge is mostly academic.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Gains knowledge of golem construction. Can animate stone constructs with basic commands.

name: Ancient Read
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Reads and interprets the ancient inscriptions found on Shudon and related relics. At its most basic, the read can decipher simple inscriptions and identify common symbols. Complex texts require extensive study.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Reads any ancient text, even in dead languages. Reveals hidden meanings and subtext.

name: Stone Whisper
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Attempts to sense residual will or traces of the world core inside dormant Shudon through physical contact. At its most basic, the whisper provides faint impressions — emotions, images, or sounds. The contact must be sustained.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Communicates with stone and earth. Can ask about recent events at the current location.

name: World Record
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Comprehensive knowledge of the Shudon's historical role in the division of the realms. At its most basic, the record covers the major events and their significance. The knowledge is essential for understanding reactivation.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Accesses the World Core’s memory of any location. Sees events that happened there centuries ago.

name: Awaken Theory
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Develops and refines theoretical methods that might one day allow reactivation of the Shudon. At its most basic, the theory is speculative — logical but unproven. Each theory requires extensive research and documentation.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Studies a creature or object to understand its fundamental nature. Reveals weaknesses and resistances.

name: Keepers Archive
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Organizes and preserves the collective research, observations, and theories of all previous Shudonkeepers. At its most basic, the archive can catalog and retrieve information efficiently. The archive grows with each generation.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Accesses a vast mental library of all recorded knowledge. Can research any topic for 5 minutes.

name: Relic Sense
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Detects and identifies Shudon-related relics and materials even when heavily damaged or buried. At its most basic, the sense covers a moderate radius and can distinguish Shudon materials from ordinary stone. The sense feels like a faint vibration.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Detects magical artifacts within 100 meters. Reveals their approximate power level.

name: Core Glimpse
subtitle: Shudonkeeper skill
description: Allows brief, incomplete glimpses of residual world-core patterns still present inside Shudon remains. At its most basic, the glimpse provides a flash of insight — a single image or feeling. The glimpse is disorienting and cannot be controlled.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Glimpses the World Core’s consciousness. Gains a random piece of cosmic knowledge.

name: Alchemist — Potion Mastery Ranks
subtitle: Alchemy progression system
description: Alchemists progress through ranks based on their brewing skill, ingredient knowledge, and ability to handle dangerous reactions. Each rank unlocks access to more complex recipes and rare ingredients. The ranks are: Distiller → Admixtor → Brewer → Compounder → Transmuter → Elixir Lord → Grand Alchemist. At Distiller, an Alchemist can make basic healing tonics. By Grand Alchemist, they can brew legendary potions like the Ethereal Potion and handle pixie dust without neutralizing it.

fields.label: Ranks
fields.value: Distiller → Admixtor → Brewer → Compounder → Transmuter → Elixir Lord → Grand Alchemist

fields.label: Distiller
fields.value: Basic tonics, simple healing drinks, identifies common ingredients

fields.label: Admixtor
fields.value: Compound potions, basic poisons, can handle minor Veyn-infused ingredients

fields.label: Brewer
fields.value: Advanced potions, explosive mixtures, works with pixie dust under supervision

fields.label: Compounder
fields.value: Multi-ingredient brews, catalyst creation, transmutation of base materials

fields.label: Transmuter
fields.value: Changes physical properties of ingredients, creates Veyn-enhanced compounds

fields.label: Elixir Lord
fields.value: Legendary-rank potions, handles dragon heart and Grimbough leaves independently

fields.label: Grand Alchemist
fields.value: Can brew the Ethereal Potion, creates entirely new formulas, master of all alchemical arts

name: Beastmaster — Bond Depth Stages
subtitle: Beastmaster progression system
description: Beastmasters progress not by raw power but by the depth and quality of their bond with creatures. Each stage represents a deeper telepathic and spiritual connection. The stages are: Whisperer → Bonded → Twin-Soul → Pack Leader → Wild Sovereign → Beastlord → Alpha Eternal. At Whisperer, a Beastmaster can sense a creature's emotions. At Alpha Eternal, they can bond with multiple apex creatures simultaneously and share their senses as if they were their own body.

fields.label: Stages
fields.value: Whisperer → Bonded → Twin-Soul → Pack Leader → Wild Sovereign → Beastlord → Alpha Eternal

fields.label: Whisperer
fields.value: Can sense creature emotions, forms basic telepathic link with willing animals

fields.label: Bonded
fields.value: Full telepathic bond with one creature, can issue basic commands in combat

fields.label: Twin-Soul
fields.value: Shares senses with bonded creature, can channel Ren into it for temporary boosts

fields.label: Pack Leader
fields.value: Bonds with multiple creatures, coordinates them in battle, creatures evolve faster

fields.label: Wild Sovereign
fields.value: Bonds with magical and rare creatures, can calm hostile beasts through the bond

fields.label: Beastlord
fields.value: Bonds with apex-tier creatures, shared abilities between master and beast

fields.label: Alpha Eternal
fields.value: Permanent multi-creature bond network, creatures retain former abilities, master and beasts share damage

name: Smithing — Forge Mastery Tiers
subtitle: Smithing progression system
description: Smiths advance through tiers based on their ability to work increasingly rare and dangerous materials, and the complexity of enchantments they can forge. The tiers are: Apprentice Smith → Metalwright → Forgemaster → Bloodforger → Runesmith → Mythic Forger → Grand Forger. At Apprentice Smith, they shape basic steel. At Grand Forger, they can work Divine materials, create legendary weapons, and handle mixed angel-demon blood without dying.

fields.label: Tiers
fields.value: Apprentice Smith → Metalwright → Forgemaster → Bloodforger → Runesmith → Mythic Forger → Grand Forger

fields.label: Apprentice Smith
fields.value: Shapes basic steel, creates functional weapons and armor with basic Veyn reinforcement

fields.label: Metalwright
fields.value: Veyn infusion during forging, creates minor magical properties, handles Ren channeling

fields.label: Forgemaster
fields.value: Creates enchanted weapons, blood-forging with low-rank blood, armor that absorbs impacts

fields.label: Bloodforger
fields.value: Works with high-rank demon and angel blood, creates weapons that can kill immortal beings

fields.label: Runesmith
fields.value: Fuses complex enchantments directly into metal, creates multi-layered weapon properties

fields.label: Mythic Forger
fields.value: Creates legendary-grade weapons, works with rare materials impossible for lesser smiths

fields.label: Grand Forger
fields.value: Can mix angel and demon blood, creates Divine-tier weapons, masters all forging disciplines

name: Enchanter — Rune Mastery Grades
subtitle: Enchanter progression system
description: Enchanters advance through grades based on their understanding of magical resonance and their ability to layer, fuse, and create enchantments. The grades are: Rune Reader → Ensorceler → Glyphwright → Wardweaver → Rune Lord → Rune Sage → Rune Transcendent. At Rune Reader, they can identify existing enchantments. At Rune Transcendent, they can create adaptive enchantments that evolve over time and develop entirely new forms of magic.

fields.label: Grades
fields.value: Rune Reader → Ensorceler → Glyphwright → Wardweaver → Rune Lord → Rune Sage → Rune Transcendent

fields.label: Rune Reader
fields.value: Identifies enchantments on items, reads their function and strength

fields.label: Ensorceler
fields.value: Creates simple lasting enchantments on ordinary items

fields.label: Glyphwright
fields.value: Channels Veyn into finished items, creates stronger magical effects

fields.label: Wardweaver
fields.value: Fuses compatible enchantments, removes and enhances existing ones

fields.label: Rune Lord
fields.value: Creates defensive and offensive trigger enchantments, layers complex effects

fields.label: Rune Sage
fields.value: Develops new enchantment patterns, creates adaptive enchantments

fields.label: Rune Transcendent
fields.value: Creates enchantments that respond to threats and evolve over time, pioneers new magical forms

name: Diviner — Sight Depth Levels
subtitle: Diviner progression system
description: Diviners advance through levels of Sight Depth — how deeply they can perceive the threads of fate, truth, and Veyn. The levels are: Insight → Reader → Watcher → Seer → Oracle → Prophet → Fatesight. At Insight, they detect obvious lies. At Fatesight, they perceive the emotional and magical bonds connecting all living things and can temporarily combine all divination effects at once.

fields.label: Levels
fields.value: Insight → Reader → Watcher → Seer → Oracle → Prophet → Fatesight

fields.label: Insight
fields.value: Detects obvious lies, basic True-Sight, senses strong Veyn presence

fields.label: Reader
fields.value: Sees through magical concealment, detects hidden beings, reads basic auras

fields.label: Watcher
fields.value: Views past events at a location, detects lies in real-time, senses Veyn density

fields.label: Seer
fields.value: Glimpses fragmented futures, reads detailed auras, prepares basic divination rituals

fields.label: Oracle
fields.value: Clearer future visions, deep past sight, protects mind from other Diviners

fields.label: Prophet
fields.value: Reliable future sight, perceives bonds between people, performs complex rituals

fields.label: Fatesight
fields.value: Combines all divination effects, perceives the interconnected web of all living things

name: Exorcist — Purification Stages
subtitle: Exorcist progression system
description: Exorcists advance through stages of purification mastery — how cleanly and powerfully they can cleanse corruption, bind fallen beings, and seal dangerous entities. The stages are: Cleaner → Warder → Binder → Purifier → Consecrator → Grand Exorcist → Eternal Seal-Bearer. At Cleaner, they remove surface miasma. At Eternal Seal-Bearer, they can place permanent suppressions on extreme corruption and banish powerful spirits.

fields.label: Stages
fields.value: Cleaner → Warder → Binder → Purifier → Consecrator → Grand Exorcist → Eternal Seal-Bearer

fields.label: Cleaner
fields.value: Removes surface miasma and minor corruption from people and objects

fields.label: Warder
fields.value: Creates barriers of purified Veyn, stabilizes chaotic Veyn in areas

fields.label: Binder
fields.value: Uses binding techniques to suppress Fallen Angels and powerful corrupted beings

fields.label: Purifier
fields.value: Performs formal exorcism rituals, cleanses deep contamination and curses

fields.label: Consecrator
fields.value: Purified Veyn strikes deal heavy damage to corrupted beings, handles mass contamination

fields.label: Grand Exorcist
fields.value: Mass purifications, banishes powerful spirits, cleanses entire regions

fields.label: Eternal Seal-Bearer
fields.value: Places permanent suppressions on extreme corruption, forces spirits to disperse permanently

name: Broker — Contract Tier Ranks
subtitle: Broker progression system
description: Brokers advance through ranks based on the complexity and stakes of the contracts they can handle. The ranks are: Clerk → Scribe → Notary → Mediator → Arbiter → Grand Arbiter → Iron Sovereign. At Clerk, they draft basic trade agreements. At Iron Sovereign, they can create contracts so binding they are nearly impossible to break, enforce penalties across realms, and mediate between rulers.

fields.label: Ranks
fields.value: Clerk → Scribe → Notary → Mediator → Arbiter → Grand Arbiter → Iron Sovereign

fields.label: Clerk
fields.value: Drafts basic trade agreements, reads simple contracts, detects obvious loopholes

fields.label: Scribe
fields.value: Creates magically binding contracts, identifies hidden clauses, basic enforcement

fields.label: Notary
fields.value: Mediates between hostile parties, creates multi-term contracts with penalties

fields.label: Mediator
fields.value: Handles high-stakes contracts with demons, enforces cross-realm agreements

fields.label: Arbiter
fields.value: Creates ironclad contracts, can forcibly dissolve dangerous agreements, network across realms

fields.label: Grand Arbiter
fields.value: Handles ruler-level disputes, creates contracts that bind entire organizations

fields.label: Iron Sovereign
fields.value: Creates near-unbreakable contracts, enforces penalties across all three realms, mediates between the Four Rulers

name: Saintess — Radiance Ascension
subtitle: Saintess progression system
description: Saintesses advance through stages of Holy Energy mastery — how purely and powerfully they can channel divine light. The stages are: Dawnlight → Glow → Radiance → Brilliance → Blazing Light → Divine Radiance → Seraphic Aura. At Dawnlight, they emit a faint healing warmth. At Seraphic Aura, they become a beacon of golden light that can selectively heal or harm, purify without damaging, and create barriers that adapt to incoming threats.

fields.label: Stages
fields.value: Dawnlight → Glow → Radiance → Brilliance → Blazing Light → Divine Radiance → Seraphic Aura

fields.label: Dawnlight
fields.value: Emits faint healing warmth, basic wound mending, weak corruption resistance

fields.label: Glow
fields.value: Heals serious wounds, creates small Holy Energy barriers, cleanses curses

fields.label: Radiance
fields.value: Channels focused Holy Energy, burns undead on contact, creates lasting holy wards

fields.label: Brilliance
fields.value: Purifies miasma and corruption, creates radiant shields, boosts ally Veyn recovery

fields.label: Blazing Light
fields.value: Heavy damage to demons and undead, reveals hidden beings, creates large holy zones

fields.label: Divine Radiance
fields.value: Selectively heals or harms, creates adaptive barriers, advanced holy techniques

fields.label: Seraphic Aura
fields.value: All holy abilities enhanced to maximum, produces effects beyond normal class limits

name: Clergy — Healing Mastery Ranks
subtitle: Clergy progression system
description: Clergy advance through ranks based on their healing skill, from basic wound care to life-saving mastery. The ranks are: Acolyte → Mercyward → Restorer → Healer → High Healer → Saint Healer → Life Weaver. At Acolyte, they can bandage wounds and apply basic Veyn. At Life Weaver, they can restore lost limbs, pull someone back from the edge of death, and develop entirely new healing techniques.

fields.label: Ranks
fields.value: Acolyte → Mercyward → Restorer → Healer → High Healer → Saint Healer → Life Weaver

fields.label: Acolyte
fields.value: Basic wound care, applies Veyn to minor cuts and bruises, first aid

fields.label: Mercyward
fields.value: Heals broken bones and deep lacerations, creates healing barriers for allies

fields.label: Restorer
fields.value: Heals internal damage, performs healing rituals, places healing wards on locations

fields.label: Healer
fields.value: One of the seven official Healers, heals serious injuries, accelerates natural recovery

fields.label: High Healer
fields.value: Heals near-fatal wounds, develops specialized treatments, trains other Clergy

fields.label: Saint Healer
fields.value: Restores lost limbs with rare components, pulls people back from death's edge

fields.label: Life Weaver
fields.value: Creates entirely new healing techniques, masters all healing disciplines, legendary healing

name: Archer — Shot Mastery Tiers
subtitle: Archer progression system
description: Archers advance through tiers based on their ability to enchant arrows and shoot with precision. The tiers are: Marksman → Sharpshooter → Enchanter Archer → Spell Archer → Storm Archer → Void Archer → Trueshot. At Marksman, they fire basic Veyn-enchanted arrows. At Trueshot, they create entirely new forms of magical ammunition and fire with perfect accuracy at impossible ranges.

fields.label: Tiers
fields.value: Marksman → Sharpshooter → Enchanter Archer → Spell Archer → Storm Archer → Void Archer → Trueshot

fields.label: Marksman
fields.value: Basic Veyn arrow enchantment, fires with good accuracy, simple elemental effects

fields.label: Sharpshooter
fields.value: Piercing and explosive arrows, improved range and precision, basic arrow shielding

fields.label: Enchanter Archer
fields.value: Homing arrows, complex enchantment combinations, arrow rain volleys

fields.label: Spell Archer
fields.value: Multi-effect arrows, healing arrows, extreme-range precision shooting

fields.label: Storm Archer
fields.value: Devastating arrow barrages, arrow constructs that hover and fire on command

fields.label: Void Archer
fields.value: Arrows that pierce through dimensions, reality-bending enchantments

fields.label: Trueshot
fields.value: Creates entirely new magical ammunition, perfect accuracy at any range, arrows that never miss

name: Paladin — Oath Ascension
subtitle: Paladin progression system
description: Paladins advance through stages of Oath power — how deeply their Auric Ren is tied to their sacred vow. The stages are: Sworn → Oathbound → Blessed → Consecrated → Divine Champion → Seraphic Knight → Eternal Guardian. At Sworn, they can channel basic Auric Ren. At Eternal Guardian, they become a beacon of golden light that inspires allies and terrifies corrupted beings, with all abilities enhanced to their absolute peak.

fields.label: Stages
fields.value: Sworn → Oathbound → Blessed → Consecrated → Divine Champion → Seraphic Knight → Eternal Guardian

fields.label: Sworn
fields.value: Basic Auric Ren strikes, weak golden shield, minor ally healing

fields.label: Oathbound
fields.value: Stronger golden attacks, heals allies while burning corrupted beings

fields.label: Blessed
fields.value: Aura of courage bolsters allies, powerful smite attacks, consecrated ground

fields.label: Consecrated
fields.value: Divine wards protect allies automatically, lays hands for deep healing

fields.label: Divine Champion
fields.value: Oath surge boosts power when allies are in danger, radiant barrier

fields.label: Seraphic Knight
fields.value: All paladin abilities enhanced, becomes a beacon of golden light

fields.label: Eternal Guardian
fields.value: Full temporary empowerment, all abilities at maximum, inspires allies and terrifies corruption

name: Grimtender — Death Mastery Ranks
subtitle: Grimtender progression system
description: Grimtenders advance through ranks based on their command over death and undeath. The ranks are: Bonewright → Gravekeeper → Bonewarden → Deathcaller → Necromancer → Grave Lord → Death Sovereign. At Bonewright, they can reanimate simple remains. At Death Sovereign, they command permanent high-quality undead, maintain large-scale simultaneous control, and can harvest souls for later use.

fields.label: Ranks
fields.value: Bonewright → Gravekeeper → Bonewarden → Deathcaller → Necromancer → Grave Lord → Death Sovereign

fields.label: Bonewright
fields.value: Reanimates simple remains, issues basic commands, uses remains as disposable shields

fields.label: Gravekeeper
fields.value: Controls multiple undead, drains Veyn from corpses, basic necrotic pulses

fields.label: Bonewarden
fields.value: Binds spirits to remains for smarter undead, creates bone projectiles

fields.label: Deathcaller
fields.value: Reanimates large groups, creates undead legions, enhanced necrotic attacks

fields.label: Necromancer
fields.value: Powerful undead that retain former abilities, large-scale simultaneous control

fields.label: Grave Lord
fields.value: Permanent undead army, harvests souls for later use, commands elite undead

fields.label: Death Sovereign
fields.value: Controls multiple powerful undead simultaneously, maintains permanent undead guard, harvests residual essence

name: Bladesinger — Blade Harmony Stages
subtitle: Bladesinger progression system
description: Bladesingers advance through stages of blade-Ren harmony — how perfectly their body, blade, and Ren flow as one. The stages are: Novice Blade → Swift Blade → Crimson Blade → Storm Blade → Phantom Blade → Eternal Blade → Perfect Edge. At Novice Blade, they perform basic sword strikes. At Perfect Edge, every movement is optimal, every defense flawless, and the blade becomes an extension of their soul.

fields.label: Stages
fields.value: Novice Blade → Swift Blade → Crimson Blade → Storm Blade → Phantom Blade → Eternal Blade → Perfect Edge

fields.label: Novice Blade
fields.value: Basic sword strikes, simple Ren coating on blade, rapid sweeping attacks

fields.label: Swift Blade
fields.value: Enhanced speed and blade dance, Ren edge cuts through harder materials

fields.label: Crimson Blade
fields.value: Powerful counter-strikes, wind step for instant closing, ghost cut from unexpected angles

fields.label: Storm Blade
fields.value: Tempest slash whirlwinds, passive grace enhances balance and reaction

fields.label: Phantom Blade
fields.value: Bladesong state enhances all physical abilities, near-invisible blade movements

fields.label: Eternal Blade
fields.value: Becomes one with the blade, executes techniques with perfect precision

fields.label: Perfect Edge
fields.value: Every movement optimal, zero wasted motion, blade is extension of soul

name: Berserker — Rage Ascension
subtitle: Berserker progression system
description: Berserkers advance through stages of rage mastery — how deeply they can tap into their Ren-fueled fury without losing themselves. The stages are: Rageborn → Bloodrager → Wrathbringer → Battlegraced → Berserk → Warlord → Avatar of War. At Rageborn, they enter controlled rage for strength boosts. At Avatar of War, their roar distorts the air, shatters structures, and empowers allies while crushing enemy morale.

fields.label: Stages
fields.value: Rageborn → Bloodrager → Wrathbringer → Battlegraced → Berserk → Warlord → Avatar of War

fields.label: Rageborn
fields.value: Controlled rage increases strength and pain tolerance, basic war howl

fields.label: Bloodrager
fields.value: Stronger rage surges, devastating single attacks, Ren burst for area damage

fields.label: Wrathbringer
fields.value: Fights through wounds that would stop others, powerful crippling blows

fields.label: Battlegraced
fields.value: Full berserk mode increases strength and speed dramatically, rage burst knocks back enemies

fields.label: Berserk
fields.value: Massive power increase, all rage abilities enhanced, fights past death's threshold

fields.label: Warlord
fields.value: Roar empowers allies and crushes enemy morale, war cry staggers entire armies

fields.label: Avatar of War
fields.value: Final rage burst on death deals catastrophic damage, all abilities at absolute peak

name: Sentinel — Guardian Oath Ranks
subtitle: Sentinel progression system
description: Sentinels advance through ranks based on their protective ability and endurance. The ranks are: Guard → Shield Bearer → Warden → Bulwark Knight → Citadel → Immortal Guardian → Eternal Sentinel. At Guard, they reinforce armor with Ren. At Eternal Sentinel, they become a wide-area defensive bastion, taking drastically reduced damage and protecting a large zone around them.

fields.label: Ranks
fields.value: Guard → Shield Bearer → Warden → Bulwark Knight → Citadel → Immortal Guardian → Eternal Sentinel

fields.label: Guard
fields.value: Reinforces armor with Ren, creates basic Ren walls, taunts enemies

fields.label: Shield Bearer
fields.value: Fortress stance makes them immovable, shield slam stuns enemies

fields.label: Warden
fields.value: Extends protective aura to allies, absorbs portion of ally damage

fields.label: Bulwark Knight
fields.value: Designates ally to protect, automatically intercepts attacks aimed at them

fields.label: Citadel
fields.value: Survives lethal damage once per battle, fights through severe injury

fields.label: Immortal Guardian
fields.value: Wide-area defensive bastion, takes drastically reduced damage

fields.label: Eternal Sentinel
fields.value: Becomes immovable wall, protects large zone, inspires allies to fight harder

name: Ren Archer — Bow Mastery Stages
subtitle: Ren Archer progression system
description: Ren Archers advance through stages of Ren-bow synchronization — how perfectly they can channel Ren through their arrows. The stages are: Novice Archer → Ren Touched → Crimson Archer → Storm Bow → Phantom Archer → Bloodshot → Arrow Sovereign. At Novice Archer, they coat arrows in basic Ren. At Arrow Sovereign, they fire with perfect accuracy while moving, create hovering arrow constructs, and imbue multiple arrows with different Ren effects.

fields.label: Stages
fields.value: Novice Archer → Ren Touched → Crimson Archer → Storm Bow → Phantom Archer → Bloodshot → Arrow Sovereign

fields.label: Novice Archer
fields.value: Basic Ren-coated arrows, increased force and penetration, rapid volley

fields.label: Ren Touched
fields.value: Power shots pierce multiple targets, armor-breaking arrows, windstep repositioning

fields.label: Crimson Archer
fields.value: Long-range precision shots, dense arrow barrages, Ren-enhanced dodging

fields.label: Storm Bow
fields.value: Enhanced vision and tracking, multiple arrow types, devastating area volleys

fields.label: Phantom Archer
fields.value: Perfect accuracy at extreme range, arrows that adjust mid-flight

fields.label: Bloodshot
fields.value: Arrows that pierce through dimensions, reality-bending Ren effects

fields.label: Arrow Sovereign
fields.value: Perfect accuracy while moving, hovering arrow constructs, multiple simultaneous Ren effects

name: Veilrunner — Shadow Mastery Tiers
subtitle: Veilrunner progression system
description: Veilrunners advance through tiers of shadow mastery — how completely they can disappear into darkness and strike without being detected. The tiers are: Nightwalker → Phantom → Ghost → Wraith → Shadow Lord → Living Shadow. At Nightwalker, they suppress sound and move quietly. At Living Shadow, they become one with the shadows, moving silently and invisibly at full speed, leaving no trace.

fields.label: Tiers
fields.value: Nightwalker → Phantom → Ghost → Wraith → Shadow Lord → Living Shadow

fields.label: Nightwalker
fields.value: Suppresses sound and moves through dim light nearly unseen, with enhanced reflexes, lock picking with Ren, and poison blade coating.

fields.label: Phantom
fields.value: High-damage backstasts, smoke screen for escape, basic disguise

fields.label: Ghost
fields.value: Full evasion mastery, Ren-enhanced dodging, vanishes for short periods

fields.label: Wraith
fields.value: Near-invisible at full speed, advanced disguise, lock touch without tools

fields.label: Shadow Lord
fields.value: Permanent shadow integration, strikes without detection, leaves no trace

fields.label: Living Shadow
fields.value: One with shadows, near-perfect stealth at full speed, vanishes indefinitely

name: Shudonkeeper — Knowledge Depths
subtitle: Shudonkeeper progression system
description: Shudonkeepers advance through depths of knowledge about the Shudon and the world core. The depths are: Student → Antiquarian → Lorekeeper → Archivist → Scholar → Sage → Core-Seer. At Student, they learn basic Shudon construction. At Core-Seer, they can sense residual world-core patterns inside Shudon remains and glimpse the true nature of the golems.

fields.label: Depths
fields.value: Student → Antiquarian → Lorekeeper → Archivist → Scholar → Sage → Core-Seer

fields.label: Student
fields.value: Learns basic Shudon construction, identifies age and origin of fragments

fields.label: Antiquarian
fields.value: Repairs inactive Shudon, reads ancient inscriptions, studies golem lore

fields.label: Lorekeeper
fields.value: Deep knowledge of Shudon creation, comprehends realm history, maintains archives

fields.label: Archivist
fields.value: Organizes all Shudon research, develops reactivation theories, senses dormant will

fields.label: Scholar
fields.value: Expert on world core's role, reads complex ancient scripts, teaches others

fields.label: Sage
fields.value: Communes with Shudon through physical contact, senses faint world-core traces

fields.label: Core-Seer
fields.value: Glimpses residual world-core patterns, deepest understanding of Shudon purpose

name: Silver Concord
subtitle: Mercenary and Contract Guild — Human Realm
description: Silver Concord is one of the most respected guilds in the Human Realm, specializing in contract mediation, mercenary dispatch, and Cross-realm trade facilitation. Founded by a B-rank Broker who saw the need for a neutral organization that could handle deals between humans, demons, and angels without bias. The guild operates out of a fortified manor in Aldermere, with branches in major cities across the Human Realm. Its reputation is built on one iron rule: every contract signed under Silver Concord's seal is honored.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: Mercenary and Contract Guild

fields.label: Location
fields.value: Aldermere, Human Realm (main branch)

fields.label: Founded
fields.value: Approximately 200 years ago

fields.label: Guildmaster
fields.value: Varen Ashtail — Broker class, B-rank

fields.label: Members
fields.value: ~150 active members across all ranks

fields.label: Specialization
fields.value: Contract mediation, mercenary dispatch, Cross-realm trade

fields.label: Reputation
fields.value: Known for ironclad fairness and reliable contract enforcement

fields.label: Guild Rules
fields.value: 1. Every contract under Silver Concord's seal is honored. 2. No member may break a signed contract. 3. The guild does not take sides in disputes. 4. Members protect each other. 5. The Guildmaster's word is final.

name: Silver Concord — Guild Ranks
subtitle: The adventurer ranks — metal on the badge
description: Silver Concord ranks its members by the classic metal tiers of an adventurer guild, earned through completed quests, proven skill, and a reputation the guild is willing to stand behind. The metal on a member’s badge is their record made visible — it opens doors, sets the price on their head, and decides which jobs they are trusted with. Rank is skill, not power, and not class: a Broker and a Bladesinger rise and fall by the same metal.

fields.label: Ranks
fields.value: Copper → Bronze → Iron → Silver → Gold → Platinum → Mithril → Guildmaster

fields.label: Copper
fields.value: Untested newcomers on their first jobs. Supervised on simple quests — escort work, pest clearing, courier runs.

fields.label: Bronze
fields.value: Proven enough to take standard quests alone. Handles routine monster hunts, retrieval jobs, and low-risk Cross-realm work.

fields.label: Iron
fields.value: Reliable veterans trusted with dangerous jobs and small team leads. Mentors the lower ranks between contracts.

fields.label: Silver
fields.value: Seasoned mercenaries who lead teams and take on high-stakes quests. Their name alone is worth a deposit.

fields.label: Gold
fields.value: Elite members sent on the guild’s most dangerous commissions — ruins, high-rank monsters, and sensitive retrievals.

fields.label: Platinum
fields.value: Legendary mercenaries whose deeds are recorded in the Archive. Handled ruler-level jobs and represent the guild to crowns.

fields.label: Mithril
fields.value: The rarest rank — a handful of living legends. Only they may take the guild’s unlisted, highest-risk contracts.

fields.label: Guildmaster
fields.value: A single, unique rank held by Varen Ashtail. Leads the guild and has the final word on every job, price, and dispute.

name: Silver Concord — Guild Facilities
subtitle: Guild amenities and resources
description: The Silver Concord main branch in Aldermere is a fortified manor that serves as both headquarters and meeting place. It contains all the facilities a guild needs to operate across the Human Realm.

fields.label: Contract Hall
fields.value: Central meeting room where contracts are drafted, reviewed, and sealed with the guild's magical imprint

fields.label: Training Grounds
fields.value: Indoor and outdoor areas for members to practice combat, negotiation, and contract enforcement

fields.label: Archive
fields.value: Vast library of completed contracts, legal precedents, and Cross-realm trade regulations

fields.label: Armory
fields.value: Weapons and armor available for members, including blood-forged weapons for high-rank missions

fields.label: Healing Ward
fields.value: Staffed by Clergy members, provides treatment for injured members

fields.label: Teleportation Circle
fields.value: Rare magical circle that allows fast travel to branch offices in other cities

fields.label: Guild Vault
fields.value: Secure storage for valuable contract items, rare ingredients, and guild funds

name: Varen Ashtail
subtitle: Guildmaster of Silver Concord — Broker class, B-rank
description: Varen Ashtail is the founder and Guildmaster of Silver Concord, a B-rank Broker who built the guild from nothing into one of the most respected organizations in the Human Realm. He is a tall, lean man in his late 40s with silver-streaked black hair and sharp grey eyes that miss nothing. He speaks softly but carries an air of absolute authority — the kind of man who can silence a room with a look. His specialty is high-stakes contract mediation, particularly deals involving demons and angels. He has never broken a contract in his life, and he expects the same of his members. Behind his calm exterior lies a man who has seen the worst of跨-realm politics and survived by being smarter, more prepared, and more principled than everyone around him.

fields.label: Class
fields.value: Broker

fields.label: Grade
fields.value: B Grade

fields.label: Guild Rank
fields.value: Guildmaster

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Late 40s

fields.label: Appearance
fields.value: Tall, lean, silver-streaked black hair, sharp grey eyes

fields.label: Personality
fields.value: Calm, authoritative, principled, observant, strategic

fields.label: Specialty
fields.value: High-stakes contract mediation,跨-realm deals

fields.label: Notable Skills
fields.value: Balance, Bindword, Loophole, Contract Break, Silver Tongue, Falsesense, Backlash Guard, Web, Pressure, Ironword

fields.label: Background
fields.value: Founded Silver Concord ~200 years ago. Built it from a small mediation office into a跨-realm guild. Has mediated between rulers and never lost a client.

fields.label: Reputation
fields.value: Known as 'The Silver Tongue' — the most trusted Broker in the Human Realm

fields.label: Sub-stage
fields.value: Mid

name: Eva Aldermere Divina
subtitle: Daughter of Ruby Divina — Mage
description: The daughter of Ruby Divina, ruler of the Human Realm. She was given the class of Mage and attends Elyndor Academy alongside Jaiden Marlock.

fields.label: Class
fields.value: Mage

fields.label: Race
fields.value: Human

fields.label: Parent
fields.value: Ruby Divina

name: Bella Rose
subtitle: Jaiden’s childhood friend — Archer with unusual holy energy
description: Jaiden Marlock’s childhood friend, and a Malakhim angel. She was given the class of Archer and attends Elyndor Academy. Jaiden gave her the bow Aerendrel, the Skybound Wrath. Bella was born with an unusually large reservoir of holy energy — far more than any Malakhim should possess at her age, and enough that even senior angels noticed it during her awakening at the Sundering Altar. The reason traces back to the night she was born: Jaiden Marlock, the first angel-demon hybrid, came into the world the same night. The world core’s will — which has no mind but acts to maintain balance — sensed the existence of a being who carried both angelic and demonic aura simultaneously, something the world had never seen and its balance had never accounted for. In response, the core’s will did what it always does when equilibrium is threatened: it pushed back. Not with thought, not with intent, but with a reflexive surge of purified Veyn that flooded the nearest compatible vessel — a newborn Malakhim angel lying in the same ward, in the same city, at the same moment. Bella Rose absorbed that surge without knowing it, and it settled into her Veyn channels as though it had always been there. She has never been told why her holy energy burns brighter than others of her rank. The Headmaster suspects the truth but has said nothing, because revealing it would mean revealing Jaiden’s nature — and the world core’s response to it — to people who would not understand what that balance means. Bella simply trains harder than everyone else, convinced her strength is talent rather than the world’s immune system reacting to a threat it could not name.

name: Rank and Role
subtitle: Power and profession are separate
description: A rank is a measure of power, not a profession. Every angel and demon has a rank — the amount of Veyn their body holds, shown by their wings and horns — but only some choose the army. Most angels and demons are civilians: merchants, craftsmen, scholars, laborers, and tradespeople who happen to hold a high or low rank. A powerful Aetherblade Lord Angel might command the army, or might simply be a master artisan who has never held a sword; a weak Gnash might be a soldier, or might run a shop in a quiet town. Rank decides how strong you are. Role decides what you do. And because rank is power rather than duty, angels and demons of any rank are free to leave their realm and live in the Human Realm as ordinary citizens, hiding their true nature behind Dawnveil or Duskveil.

fields.label: Type
fields.value: World Mechanic - Social Structure

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Every race has rank system for social status, authority, combat capability. Earned through training, breakthroughs, achievement. Higher ranks = more powerful skills and responsibilities.

name: The Ren Organ
subtitle: How angels and demons channel Ren
description: Angels and demons are born to Veyn — their aura, halo or miasma, and every innate skill run on it — and Ren, the inner energy drawn from a body’s own Vitality, does not come naturally to them. But it is not impossible. An angel or demon can unlock a Ren Organ: a channel within the body that lets them draw on their own Vitality and use Ren the way a human or swordsman does. The cost is absolute — while the Ren Organ is open, the user cannot touch any form of Veyn at all. The moment Veyn and Ren meet inside the same body, the incompatibility rule applies and can kill them. This means an angel or demon who walks the Ren path must fight without their aura, their halo or miasma, and every innate Veyn skill they were born with, until they close the organ and return to Veyn.

fields.label: Unlock
fields.value: An angel or demon can unlock a Ren Organ to channel Ren from their own Vitality.

fields.label: Cost
fields.value: While the organ is open, the user cannot touch any form of Veyn — not even their own aura or innate skills.

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Mixing Veyn and Ren in one body applies the incompatibility rule and can kill.

name: Rune Star Circles vs Grades
subtitle: How a Mage’s circle compares to a Grade
description: Mages do not use the Grade system — their power is measured by the Rune Star Circle inscribed into their heart. But the two scales can be compared directly by the power each tier represents. A Mage’s circle is roughly equal to a Grade as follows, starting at F because a Mage is by definition already awakened to Veyn (no Mage sits at G Grade, which means never exposed to Veyn).

fields.label: 1st Circle (Initiate)
fields.value: ≈ F Grade — the foundation stage; basic spells and control

fields.value: ≈ D Grade — competent and self-sufficient; most adventurers

fields.label: 4th Circle (Warden)
fields.value: ≈ C Grade — can level structures and command real force

fields.label: 5th Circle (Archmage)
fields.value: ≈ B Grade — city-destroying power; terrain shaping

name: Aldric Malgrave
subtitle: The Former King of the Human Realm
description: Aldric Malgrave was the ruler of the Human Realm before the Divina line, and the man whose fear ended a race. He looked on the Aelthar — the ancient realm-makers who could shape and tear reality itself — and saw not a people but a threat to his crown, and he hunted them to extinction. His persecution drove the survivors to tear open the Hidden Realm as a refuge, an act so violent it nearly unmade the world and forced the world core’s will to raise the barrier that split the realms apart. He caught every one of them but one — Kael von Ashen, the sole survivor who would become Headmaster of Elyndor Academy — and that single failure is the thread the whole story hangs from.

name: The Rarity of Generals
subtitle: Why a general is a rare sight
description: The generals of the Angel and Demon Realms — the Six Pillars of Angels and the demon generals of the Demon army — are so few, and so elevated, that most people go their whole lives without ever seeing one. To the ordinary angel or demon, catching sight of a general is like a common citizen glimpsing the ruler of a country: a moment of awe, of stillness, of wanting to be near the power without ever daring to be in its way. It is not merely rank that sets them apart, but distance — they are the apex of realms whose populations number in the tens or hundreds of thousands, and they are seen only in war, in council, or in legend. When one appears, the crowd remembers it for the rest of their lives. Yet not every general is a hermit. A few of them — never most, and never often — take little strolls through their realm, walking among the people who would never otherwise see them. Those walks are quiet, unannounced, and rare; the people who glimpse them remember it for the rest of their lives too.

fields.value: Seeing one is like glimpsing a head of state — a rare, awe-struck moment most people never experience.

fields.label: Strolls
fields.value: A few generals — never most, never often — take quiet, unannounced strolls through their realm.

name: Cross-Class Skills
subtitle: Why most people stick to what the altar gave them
description: Every awakened person is assigned one class at the Sundering Altar, and that class is where their path begins. Humans, unlike angels and demons, can in theory learn the skills of any class — but in the world as it is, learning a skill outside your own class is extremely difficult. The body’s Veyn is shaped to its class at awakening, and forcing it to learn a foreign discipline is slow, painful, and usually fails. Most humans who try give up. So in this era of the world, people stick to what the altar gave them — not because they are forbidden to reach for more, but because the effort is rarely worth it.

fields.label: The fact
fields.value: Humans find it difficult to learn skills from classes other than their own, so they stick to the class the altar assigned them.

fields.label: Why
fields.value: The body’s Veyn is shaped to its class at awakening; forcing a foreign discipline is slow, painful, and usually fails.

name: Skill Activation
subtitle: How skills are triggered in the Half-Made World
description:
Every skill in the Half-Made World requires three things to activate: Veyn or Ren channeling, a trigger method, and a focus. Without all three, the skill fails.

Veyn channeling is the raw fuel — pulling ambient Veyn from the surroundings or releasing stored Veyn from the body's reserves. Ren channeling works differently: instead of pulling from the outside, the user pushes their own Vitality outward, which is why Ren-based skills feel warm and physical while Veyn-based skills feel cool and ambient.

The trigger method depends on the class and the skill. Mages use verbal incantations — short phrases or words of power that focus the mind and direct the Veyn. Some Mages can skip incantations at higher Rune Star Circles, but this requires extraordinary willpower. Paladins and Berserkers use physical gestures — a sword swing, a stomp, a shout — that channel Ren outward through motion. Diviners use mental focus alone: stillness, closed eyes, and deep concentration. Alchemists require physical reagents — ingredients that react with Veyn to produce the desired effect.

The focus is the final component: the user's intent. Without clear purpose, Veyn scatters harmlessly. A Mage trying to cast a shield spell while thinking about attack will produce neither. Intent is not optional; it is the glue that holds the other two components together. Higher-grade fighters develop sharper intent, which is why their skills activate faster and hit harder even at the same Veyn level.

fields.label: Veyn Channeling
fields.value: Pulling ambient Veyn from surroundings or releasing stored Veyn from the body

fields.label: Ren Channeling
fields.value: Pushing your own Vitality outward — warm, physical, drawn from the body itself

fields.label: Trigger Methods
fields.value: Verbal incantation (Mages), physical gesture (Paladins/Berserkers), mental focus (Diviners), reagents (Alchemists)

fields.label: Focus
fields.value: Clear intent — without purpose, Veyn scatters harmlessly

fields.label: Faster Activation
fields.value: Higher-grade fighters develop sharper intent, activating skills faster

name: Veyn Combat
subtitle: How Veyn-based classes fight
description:
Veyn-based fighters — Mages, Alchemists, Enchanters, Diviners, Archers, Exorcists, Saintesses, Clergy, and Grimtenders — draw power from ambient Veyn in the environment rather than from their own bodies. This means their strength depends heavily on where they fight: a Mage standing in a Veyn-rich area near the Ether Forest is significantly more powerful than the same Mage in a barren wasteland.

During combat, a Veyn user first draws Veyn into their body through their channels — the internal pathways that carry Veyn just as veins carry blood. Once Veyn is inside, it must be shaped into the desired effect through the trigger method (incantation, gesture, or focus). Shaping takes time: a basic bolt might take half a second, while a complex barrier could take several seconds of continuous channeling.

Veyn users must manage two resources: their Veyn reserves (how much they can hold) and their channel capacity (how fast they can draw and release). A Mage with huge reserves but narrow channels will tire slowly but cast slowly. A Mage with wide channels but small reserves will cast fast but run dry quickly. Training expands both, but at different rates.

Once a skill is cast, there is a brief cooldown — the time it takes for the channels to stabilize before they can handle another burst of Veyn. During cooldown, the fighter is vulnerable. Experienced combatants learn to chain skills in rhythm, activating one skill during another's cooldown period.

fields.label: Power Source
fields.value: Ambient Veyn drawn from the environment — strength varies by location

fields.label: Veyn Channels
fields.value: Internal pathways that carry Veyn; wider channels = faster casting

fields.label: Veyn Reserves
fields.value: How much Veyn you can hold; larger reserves = longer fights

fields.label: Shaping Time
fields.value: The time between drawing Veyn and releasing the effect — half a second for bolts, seconds for barriers

fields.label: Cooldown
fields.value: Brief stabilization period between casts; skilled fighters chain skills rhythmically

fields.label: Location Dependency
fields.value: Veyn-rich areas (forests, altars) make Veyn fighters stronger; barren areas weaken them

name: Ren Combat
subtitle: How Ren-based classes fight
description:
Ren-based fighters — Bladesingers, Berserkers, Sentinels, Ren Archers, Veilrunners, Beastmasters, and Paladins — draw power from their own Vitality. Where Veyn fighters reach outward to pull magic from the world, Ren fighters push inward to burn their own life force as fuel. This makes Ren combat warm, physical, and self-destructive if overused.

A Ren user channels Vitality through their body to enhance strength, speed, endurance, or to manifest specific effects like a Berserker's rage aura or a Sentinel's iron skin. The more Vitality burned, the more powerful the effect — but Vitality is finite. A Berserker who pushes too hard into Rage will collapse from exhaustion, and a Bladesinger who burns too much Vitality mid-combo will find their sword arm going numb and their vision blurring.

Unlike Veyn fighters who can replenish from the environment, Ren fighters must rest, eat, and recover naturally. A Veyn Mage can fight for hours in a Veyn-rich area; a Ren Berserker might exhaust their Vitality in minutes of all-out combat. This is why Ren fighters favor short, decisive engagements — hit hard, hit fast, end it before the Vitality runs dry.

Paladins are the exception: their Auric Ren — Vitality brightened into gold — lets them heal and protect as well as fight, making them the longest-lasting Ren fighters. But even Paladins must eventually rest.

A critical rule: Ren fighters cannot use Veyn simultaneously. Attempting to channel both Ren and Veyn at the same time causes catastrophic internal failure and can kill. The one exception is Smithing, where a Smith may draw on both during the forge — but only during forging, never in combat.

fields.label: Power Source
fields.value: Your own Vitality — finite, warm, physical, self-destructive if overused

fields.label: Channeling
fields.value: Push Vitality through your body to enhance strength, speed, or manifest effects

fields.label: Vitality Burn
fields.value: The more you burn, the stronger the effect — but Vitality is finite

fields.label: Recovery
fields.value: Rest, food, natural recovery — no environmental replenishment unlike Veyn

fields.label: Duration
fields.value: Short decisive engagements — Ren fighters run dry faster than Veyn fighters

fields.label: Dual Channeling
fields.value: FORBIDDEN — attempting Ren + Veyn simultaneously causes death. Smithing is the sole exception

name: Holy & Corrupted Combat
subtitle: How holy and corrupted Veyn interact in battle
description:
Holy Energy and Corrupted Veyn (miasma) represent the two extreme forms of Veyn, and they interact in specific ways during combat.

Holy Energy — the purified gold form of Veyn used by angels, Saintesses, Exorcists, and Paladins — naturally burns corruption on contact. A holy strike against an undead creature or a miasma-corrupted target deals amplified damage because the purified Veyn actively unravels the corruption. Against uncorrupted targets, holy energy is no more effective than raw Veyn — it is specialized, not universally stronger.

Corrupted Veyn — the dark purple or black form used by demons — harms humans directly and can contaminate holy auras and holy energy. A demon's miasma attack against a human doesn't just damage; it begins corrupting the victim's own Veyn channels, potentially triggering Corruption Sickness if contact is prolonged. Against angels, corrupted Veyn is especially dangerous because it can destabilize their Vow, potentially leading to Fallen Angel transformation.

The interaction creates a rock-paper-scissors dynamic: Holy beats Corrupted, Corrupted harms humans and destabilizes angels, and raw Veyn is neutral against both. This is why Exorcists exist — they specialize in wielding holy energy specifically to counter corrupted threats. It is also why Vireth, the Fallen Grace, is so dangerous: its corrupted holy blade cuts through both holy and demonic wards equally, treating purified and corrupted Veyn as the same thing to sever.

Against neutral targets, all three forms of Veyn deal roughly equal damage — the advantage is purely in type matchups, not raw power.

fields.label: Holy vs Corrupted
fields.value: Holy energy burns corruption on contact — amplified damage against undead, miasma, corrupted Veyn

fields.label: Corrupted vs Humans
fields.value: Miasma harms humans and corrupts their Veyn channels — can trigger Corruption Sickness

fields.label: Corrupted vs Angels
fields.value: Destabilizes angel Vow — prolonged exposure risks Fallen Angel transformation

fields.label: Raw Veyn
fields.value: Neutral against both holy and corrupted — no special advantage or disadvantage

fields.label: Vireth Exception
fields.value: Cuts through both holy and demonic wards equally — the ultimate type-ignoring weapon

name: Grade-Based Combat Power
subtitle: How the Grade System affects fighting ability
description:
Every fighter's Grade determines their baseline power, and the gaps between grades are enormous. A single grade difference is manageable; two grade differences is dangerous; three or more is nearly insurmountable.

At F Grade (the starting point after awakening), a fighter can use basic skills but their Veyn or Ren channels are narrow, their reserves are small, and their physical capabilities are only slightly above a normal person. F Grade fighters can handle common monsters but struggle against anything aggressive.

At E Grade, the fighter's channels have widened enough to use skills reliably, and their body has been strengthened by Veyn/Ren exposure. They can fight monsters confidently and hold their own against other E-rank fighters.

D Grade is where fighters become truly dangerous. Their channels are wide, their reserves deep, and their physical capabilities far exceed normal humans. A D-rank fighter can destroy small structures and lead groups in battle.

The jumps become catastrophic above D Grade. A C-rank can destroy buildings. A B-rank can destroy cities. An A-rank is a force of nature. An S-rank is a demigod.

The practical effect in combat: a B-rank fighter facing an army of D-ranks will win without effort. The D-ranks simply cannot generate enough force to overwhelm the B-rank's defenses, while the B-rank can wipe them out with single attacks. This is why等级 gaps matter so much in the story — when Jaiden faces opponents multiple grades above him, he must use tactics, environment, and creativity rather than raw power.

fields.label: F Grade
fields.value: Starting point — basic skills, narrow channels, slightly above normal humans

fields.label: E Grade
fields.value: Reliable skill use, wider channels, confident monster fighting

fields.label: D Grade
fields.value: Truly dangerous — wide channels, deep reserves, can lead groups in battle

fields.label: C Grade
fields.value: Elite — can destroy buildings, command large groups

fields.label: B Grade
fields.value: Apex — can destroy cities, single attacks wipe out armies of lower grades

fields.label: A Grade
fields.value: Force of nature — reshape terrain, rival divine beings

fields.label: S Grade
fields.value: Demigod — nearing godhood, incomprehensible to mortals

fields.label: Gap Rule
fields.value: 1 grade difference = manageable, 2 = dangerous, 3+ = nearly insurmountable

name: Weapon Types & Class Compatibility
subtitle: What weapons each class uses and why
description:
Not every weapon works with every class. The weapon must complement the energy type the fighter uses.

Veyn-based classes favor enchanted or flexible weapons: staves, wands, bows, and catalysts that help channel ambient Veyn into shaped effects. A Mage's staff doesn't add power — it helps focus intent and provides a physical anchor for Veyn shaping. Archers use Veyn to enchant their arrows mid-flight, so their bows must be strong enough to handle the Veyn surge without breaking.

Ren-based classes favor physical weapons that can carry Vitality through contact: swords, axes, hammers, spears, and shields. A Bladesinger's sword is an extension of their body — they channel Ren through the blade itself, which is why a well-forged weapon matters enormously. Berserkers favor heavy weapons because their rage-enhanced strikes need mass behind them. Sentinels use shields because their role is to absorb and deflect.

Paladins occupy a unique position: they use swords and shields like Ren fighters, but their Auric Ren lets them imbue their weapon with holy properties — a Paladin's sword can burn undead and heal allies on contact.

Beastmasters use no weapons themselves — their bonded creature is their weapon. The bond lets them channel Ren through the creature, enhancing its natural abilities.

Smiths are the exception to all rules: they forge weapons but their weapons are tools, not extensions of themselves. A Smith's hammer channels both Veyn and Ren during forging, but once the weapon is complete, it is just metal — until someone else picks it up.

fields.label: Veyn Classes
fields.value: Staves, wands, bows, catalysts — tools to focus and channel ambient Veyn

fields.label: Ren Classes
fields.value: Swords, axes, hammers, spears — weapons that carry Vitality through physical contact

fields.label: Paladin Weapons
fields.value: Swords and shields imbued with Auric Ren — can burn undead and heal allies

fields.label: Beastmaster
fields.value: No weapons — the bonded creature is the weapon, enhanced through Ren

fields.label: Smithing
fields.value: Forge tools channel both Veyn and Ren during creation, but the finished weapon is mundane metal

fields.label: Weapon Quality
fields.value: A well-forged weapon matters enormously — poor weapons break under Veyn/Ren channeling

name: Currency System
subtitle: The coin denominations of the Half-Made World
description: The four-tier coinage system used across all realms. Copper for basics, silver for daily life, gold for significant purchases, platinum for rare high-value deals.

fields.label: Copper Coins (cc)
fields.value: Base unit. Used for small purchases — street food, basic supplies, minor services.

fields.label: Silver Coins (sc)
fields.value: 10 copper = 1 silver. Standard daily currency. Inn stays, meals, basic gear.

fields.label: Gold Coins (gc)
fields.value: 10 silver = 1 gold. Significant purchases — weapons, enchantments, Broker contracts.

fields.label: Platinum Coins (pc)
fields.value: 10 gold = 1 platinum. Rare. Used for high-value transactions — artifact deals, realm-spanning contracts.

fields.label: Exchange Rates
fields.value: 1 pc = 10 gc = 100 sc = 1,000 cc. The Sigils entry uses an older 100:1 system — disregard that; this 10:1 system is canonical.

fields.label: Black Market Premium
fields.value: Corrupted items, smuggled goods, and illegal services command 2-5x normal prices.

name: Marketplace & Trade
subtitle: How buying and selling works across the realms
description:
Each realm has its own marketplace culture shaped by what it produces and what it needs.

The Human Realm has the most developed marketplaces. Every city and town has a central market square where merchants sell everything from food to enchantments. The largest marketplace in the Human Realm is the Sunwell Market in the capital, where goods from all three realms converge. Human merchants are the backbone of cross-realm trade because they are the only race that can travel freely between all three realms without suspicion.

The Angel Realm has fewer marketplaces but more specialized ones. Angels trade through promise-based exchange rather than coin — a Lumen craftsman might create a set of enchanted tools and give them to a Virtue soldier in exchange for future protection. This works because the Vow binds them to keep their word. The exception is trade with outsiders: angels dealing with humans or demons use coin like everyone else.

The Demon Realm operates on a more brutal economy. Gnash demons run most of the marketplace stalls, selling scavenged goods, monster parts, and black market items. Currency is accepted but barter and favors are more common. The demon marketplace in the Umbrage Forest border is infamous for selling items that would be illegal elsewhere — corrupted Veyn artifacts, cursed weapons, and information.

The Hidden Realm has no permanent marketplace. The Wanderer appears randomly and sells unique artifacts at premium prices. Pixie dust and rare ingredients from the Hidden Realm are among the most valuable trade goods in the world, but obtaining them requires dangerous expeditions.

fields.label: Human Realm Markets
fields.value: Most developed — central market squares in every city; Sunwell Market is the largest

fields.label: Angel Realm Trade
fields.value: Promise-based exchange using Vow bonds; coin used only for outside trade

fields.label: Demon Realm Trade
fields.value: Gnash-run stalls, barter and favors more common than coin; black market is infamous

fields.label: Hidden Realm
fields.value: No permanent marketplace — Wanderer appears randomly selling unique artifacts

fields.label: Cross-Realm Trade
fields.value: Human merchants are the backbone — only race that travels freely between all three realms

name: Price Guide
subtitle: Every price in the Half-Made World — potions, contracts, services, and more
description:
A comprehensive reference for what things cost. All prices in standard currency (Copper Shard / Silver Mark / Gold Crown). Exchange rate: 10 cp = 1 sm, 10 sm = 1 gc, 100 cp = 1 gc.

WAGE BENCHMARKS (for context):
- Common laborer: 1-2 sm/day
- Skilled craftsman: 3-5 sm/day
- Master Smith / high-rank Alchemist: 10+ sm/day
- Academy instructor: 15-25 sm/day
- Broker (certified): 20-40 sm/day
- Realm soldier: 3-8 sm/day
- Mercenary (hired guard): 5-15 sm/day depending on danger

---

POTIONS & ELIXIRS

Healing Potion:
  - Minor (heals cuts, bruises, minor burns): 3-5 sm
  - Standard (heals broken bones, moderate wounds): 1-2 gc
  - Serious (heals severe injuries, near-fatal wounds): 5-10 gc
  - Note: Only Clergy healers can brew these. Alchemists can brew cruder versions at half price but with side effects (nausea, temporary Veyn instability).

Restoration Potion (restores Veyn reserves):
  - Small dose (restores ~20% Veyn): 10-15 gc
  - Full dose (restores ~80% Veyn): 25-40 gc
  - Note: Requires Veyn Stones as ingredients. Price fluctuates with Veyn Stone availability.

Lucent Reserve (full restoration — Veyn or Ren):
  - Single dose: 50-80 gc
  - Note: Requires Lucent Stones, which are rare and expensive. Only a few Alchemists can brew this. Often unavailable at any price.

Ethereal Potion (halts aging for a fixed period):
  - Priceless — ingredients include pixie dust, dragon heart, and Kaelroot bark. No Alchemist can guarantee success. The Wanderer occasionally has one: 500+ gc, if available at all.

Rejuvenating Elixir (complete physical heal):
  - 100-200 gc
  - Note: Can heal anything except a severed head or a missing heart past 10 minutes. Extremely rare. Only 2-3 Alchemists in the world can brew it.

Pixie Dust (raw ingredient):
  - 5-10 gc per pouch (legitimate, if you can find it)
  - 50+ gc on the black market (smuggled from Hidden Realm)
  - Note: Used in Ethereal Potion brewing. Permanent Veyn boost if consumed raw (risky — unregulated dosage).

Anti-Corruption Ward (prevents Corrupted Veyn exposure):
  - 15-25 gc per ward (lasts 24 hours)
  - Note: Essential for anyone entering the Umbrage Forest or Demon Realm border. Sold by Exorcists and select Alchemists.

Veyn Dust Explosives (combat alchemy):
  - Single charge: 3-5 gc
  - Bundle (5 charges): 12-20 gc
  - Note: Used by Alchemists in combat. Illegal in the Angel Realm.

---

BROKER CONTRACTS & SERVICES

Basic Broker Contract (simple trade agreement):
  - Broker fee: 5-10% of contract value (minimum 2 sm)
  - Veyn-seal included
  - Processing time: 1-3 days

Complex Broker Contract (multi-party, cross-realm):
  - Broker fee: 10-15% of contract value (minimum 1 gc)
  - Requires Senior Broker
  - Processing time: 3-7 days

Gnash Demon Contract (mediated through Broker):
  - Broker fee: 15-25% of contract value (minimum 5 gc)
  - Requires certified Broker with Demon Contract training
  - Risk surcharge: +5 gc if the Gnash is high-rank
  - Note: Going to a Gnash directly without a Broker is legal but extremely risky — no enforcement, no safety net.

Contract Dispute Resolution:
  - Filing fee: 10% of contract value (split between both parties)
  - Processing time: 1-3 days
  - Appeal to Guild Master: additional 5% fee

Broker Certification Examination:
  - Academy tuition (if not already enrolled): 200-500 gc
  - Examination fee: 50 gc
  - Certification fee: 25 gc/year (renewal)
  - Note: Only ~200 certified Brokers exist in the Human Realm.

Enforcement Broker Services:
  - Contract violation investigation: 10-50 gc (depending on complexity)
  - Criminal apprehension: 20-100 gc (depending on target's grade)
  - Note: Enforcement Brokers have authority to arrest anyone suspected of contract fraud.

---

MAGICAL SERVICES

Healing (Clergy/Saintess):
  - Minor healing (cuts, bruises): 3-5 sm
  - Moderate healing (broken bones, moderate wounds): 1-2 gc

name: Trade Routes
subtitle: The main paths of commerce between realms
description:
Trade between the three realms follows established routes that have existed for centuries, kept safe by mutual agreement between the rulers.

The Sunward Road is the primary trade route between the Human Realm and the Angel Realm. It runs from the capital city of the Human Realm through the neutral temple district (where the Common Altar sits) and into the Angel Realm. Caravans travel this route weekly, carrying human agricultural goods north and angel-crafted items south. The road is well-maintained and heavily patrolled — attacking a Sunward Road caravan is considered an act of war against both realms.

The Thorn Road connects the Human Realm to the Demon Realm, passing through the border regions near the Umbrage Forest. This route is far more dangerous — trolls, orcs, and other Umbrage creatures frequently raid caravans. The Demon Realm sends its trade goods (monster parts, corrupted materials, black market items) south along this route, while human merchants bring food, tools, and luxury goods north. The road has no official protection; merchants hire mercenaries or Broker-escorted convoys for safety.

The Ether Crossing is the point where the Ether Forest meets both realms — the Arubian and Umbrage halves share a border that traders occasionally cross, though this is illegal and extremely dangerous. Pallantine Elves tolerate Arubian-side trade but Veilborn Elves attack anyone crossing from the Umbrage side.

There is no direct trade route to the Hidden Realm. The portal moves every leap year, making permanent routes impossible. Traders who want Hidden Realm goods must seek out the Wanderer or mount dangerous expeditions when the portal opens.

name: The Broker's Guild
subtitle: The regulated system for handling contracts and trade
description:
The Broker's Guild is a cross-realm organization that regulates the Broker class and manages contract enforcement, particularly those involving Gnash demons. Without a Broker, making deals with demons is extremely dangerous — Gnash demons are bound by contracts they sign, but they will exploit every loophole if one exists.

The Guild operates offices in every major city across all three realms. Brokers must pass a certification process through the Guild before they can legally practice. The certification tests knowledge of contract law, demon behavior, Veyn channeling for contract seals, and ethical standards.

The Guild's primary function is mediating contracts: when a human wants to make a deal with a Gnash demon, they go to a Guild-certified Broker who drafts the contract, ensures both parties understand the terms, and applies a Veyn seal that binds both parties. Breaking a sealed contract causes physical damage to the breaker — their Veyn channels tear, causing pain and potentially permanent damage.

The Guild also handles dispute resolution, trade regulation, and information brokering. A high-ranking Broker knows the value of everything and everyone, and their network of contacts spans all three realms. Brokers are not fighters by nature, but their knowledge and connections make them invaluable allies — or dangerous enemies.

The Guild maintains strict neutrality in political conflicts. A Broker who takes sides loses their certification. This neutrality makes the Guild one of the few organizations trusted across all three realms.

name: Realm Armies
subtitle: The military forces of each realm
description:
Each realm maintains its own military force, structured differently based on the race's strengths and culture.

The Angel Army is commanded by the Six Pillars — six Aetherblade Lord Angels who serve as the highest-ranking military officers below the Serapharch. The army is small (angels barely die and do not breed quickly) but extraordinarily powerful. Every soldier is at least Virtue rank, and the average angel soldier has centuries of combat experience. The Angel Army specializes in defensive operations and rapid response — they rarely attack, but when they do, it is devastating.

The Demon Army is massive — hundreds of thousands strong, drawn from the endless breeding of the Demon Realm. It is commanded by Bloodward-rank demons and organized into war-bands led by the strongest Scourge. The army relies on sheer numbers, overwhelming force, and the demon's natural regeneration. Demons die in droves but breed fast enough to maintain their numbers. The Demon Army is the only force that can field endless waves of troops.

The Human Army is the most diverse — humans serve in every role from foot soldiers to mages to healers. It is organized into regiments commanded by D-rank or higher fighters, with Clergy healers embedded in every unit. The Human Army is the largest of the three realms but individually weaker than angel or demon forces. Its strength lies in adaptability and numbers.

All three armies maintain a tense peace enforced by the Academy's neutrality. Open war between realms would destroy the Academy and cut off magical awakening for everyone — a cost no realm is willing to pay.

name: The Seer's Order
subtitle: The hidden network that protects the Truthstone and Healer succession
description:
The Seer's Order is a small, secretive organization dedicated to protecting the Truthstone and ensuring the continuity of the seven Healers. The Order has existed for as long as the Healer system has — when one Healer dies, the current Seer uses the Truthstone to locate the next one within two years.

The Order operates in the shadows. Its members are not publicly known — they blend into ordinary society, watching for signs that the Truthstone's target is ready to be found. When the time comes, a member of the Order approaches the candidate and guides them to the Seer for confirmation.

The Order's structure is simple: one Seer (the keeper of the Truthstone), two Guardians (who protect the Seer), and a handful of Scouts (who locate and watch candidates). The Seer is always a Diviner — the only class with True-Sight, which lets them verify the Truthstone's guidance without deception.

The Order's greatest fear is the Truthstone falling into the wrong hands. If someone with malicious intent controlled the Truthstone, they could locate and kill future Healers before they are awakened, gradually destroying the Clergy class and leaving the Human Realm without magical healing. This is why the Seer's location is never revealed to anyone outside the Order.

name: The Pallantine Rangers
subtitle: The forest protectors of the Arubian Forest
description:
The Pallantine Rangers are the military and protective force of the Pallantine Elves, stationed throughout the Arubian Forest. Their primary duty is protecting the forest and its inhabitants — Fairies, Stonehollow Elk, and the ancient Thornweald-bound trees.

Rangers operate in small patrols of three to five elves, each led by a Senior Ranger. They know every path, every clearing, and every creature in the Arubian Forest. They ride Griffens for rapid response and carry enchanted longbows that channel Veyn into their arrows.

The Rangers enforce the forest's laws: no unauthorized logging, no hunting of protected species, no disturbing the Thornweald trees. Violators are warned once; a second violation results in the Ranger escorting the offender out of the forest permanently. A third violation results in the Rangers withdrawing their protection entirely, leaving the offender to the forest's natural dangers.

The Rangers also serve as the Pallantine's contact point with the outside world. They manage trade with human merchants who come to the forest's edge and coordinate with Elyndor Academy when Pallantine students need to travel for their awakening.

name: The Veyn Calendar
subtitle: The standard dating system used across all three realms
description:
The Half-Made World uses the Veyn Calendar, standardized by Elyndor Academy so all three realms share a common dating system. The calendar is divided into 12 months of 30 days each, with 5 Festival Days between months (6 at year's end for leap years). Each month is named after a significant aspect of the world.

The months are:
1. Awakening Month (when children turn 15 and go to the Altar)
2. Bloom Month (spring planting in the Human Realm)
3. Ember Month (the hottest month in the Demon Realm)
4. Hollow Month (when the Hidden Realm portal is most active)
5. Frost Month (deep winter across all realms)
6. Verdant Month (the Arubian Forest is at its most lush)
7. Shatter Month (the month of the great historical battle that destroyed the Aelthar)
8. Veil Month (when the Ether Forest boundary is thinnest)
9. Glow Month (the angels celebrate their founding)
10. Dusk Month (demons observe their remembrance of the fallen)
11. Stone Month (when Shudon activity is most detectable)
12. Renewal Month (year's end, celebrations and renewals)

The Festival Days between months are public holidays across all realms. The most significant is the Day of Sundering (between Hollow and Frost Months), which commemorates the creation of the Hidden Realm and the near-destruction of the world.
